title.raw: 卷二十六 志第六: 禮儀六 Volume 26 Treatises 6: Rites 6

sentences.zh: 志第六禮儀六

translations.literal: Treatise Six, Rites Six.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 6: Rites 6.

sentences.zh: 建中元年三月，禮儀使上言：「東都太廟闕木主，請造以祔。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Jianzhong, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "The Eastern Capital Grand Temple lacks wooden spirit tablets; we request that they be made for enshrinement."
translations.idiomatic: Third month, Jianzhong 1: the ritual commissioner reported that the Eastern Capital Grand Temple had no wooden tablets and asked that tablets be made for enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 」初，武后於東都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟。

translations.literal: Initially, Empress Wu had established temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At first Empress Wu had built three shrines at the eastern capital—for Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 至中宗已後，兩京太廟，四時並饗。

translations.literal: By the time of Zhongzong and afterward, the Grand Temples of both capitals received offerings in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhongzong onward, both capitals' ancestral halls were fed in every season.

sentences.zh: 至德亂後，木主多亡缺未祔。

translations.literal: After the rebellion of Zhide, many wooden tablets were lost or missing and had not been enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide turmoil, many tablets were lost and never re-enshrined.

sentences.zh: 於是議者紛然，而大旨有三：「其一曰，必存其廟，遍立群主，時饗之。

translations.literal: Debate erupted; the main positions were three: "First, the shrine must be kept, tablets installed for all lords, and seasonal offerings made."
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued in three camps: first, keep the temple, install tablets for all lords, and offer seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其二曰，建廟立主，存而不祭，若皇輿時巡，則就饗焉。

translations.literal: "Second, build the shrine and tablets but keep them without sacrifice; when the imperial carriage tours, feast there."
translations.idiomatic: Second, build the hall and tablets but do not sacrifice—only feast when the imperial tour came east.

sentences.zh: 其三曰，存其廟，瘞其主，駕或東幸，則飾齋車奉京師群廟之主以往。

translations.literal: "Third, keep the shrine, bury the tablets; when the throne tours east, dress a fasting carriage and bring the capital's ancestral tablets along."
translations.idiomatic: Third, keep the temple, bury the tablets, and when the throne toured east, dress a fasting carriage and bring the capital's tablets along.

sentences.zh: 議者皆不決而罷。

translations.literal: The debaters reached no decision and the matter lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Debate deadlocked and the matter lapsed.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年四月，膳部郎中歸崇敬上疏：「東都太廟，不合置木主。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, Gui Chongjing, Bureau Director of Provisions, submitted a memorial: "The Eastern Capital Grand Temple ought not to hold wooden spirit tablets."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan 15, fourth month: Gui Chongjing of the Provisions Bureau memorialized that the eastern temple ought not hold wooden tablets.

sentences.zh: 謹按典禮。

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: He cited canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 虞主用桑，練主用栗，重作栗主，則埋桑主。

translations.literal: The yu tablet uses mulberry; the lian tablet uses chestnut; when the chestnut tablet is remade, the mulberry tablet is buried.
translations.idiomatic: A yu tablet uses mulberry; a lian tablet uses chestnut—remake the chestnut tablet and bury the mulberry.

sentences.zh: 所以神無二主，猶天無二日，土無二王也。

translations.literal: Thus a spirit has no two dwelling places, as heaven has no two suns and earth no two kings.
translations.idiomatic: Thus no spirit has two abodes—no more than heaven two suns or earth two kings.

sentences.zh: 今東都太廟，是則天皇后所建，以置武氏木主。

translations.literal: Today's Eastern Capital Grand Temple was built by Empress Zetian to house the Wu clan's wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Today's eastern hall was built by Empress Wu to seat the Wu line's tablets.

sentences.zh: 中宗去其主而存其廟，蓋將以備行幸遷都之所也。

translations.literal: Zhongzong removed the tablets but kept the shrine, likely to prepare for tours or moving the seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong cleared the tablets but kept the building, preparing a site for tours or capital moves.

sentences.zh: 且殷人屢遷，前八後五，前後遷都一十三度，不可每都而別立神主也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Shang moved their seat many times—eight capitals before, five after, thirteen relocations in all—and did not erect separate spirit tablets in every city.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang moved constantly—eight capitals before, five after, thirteen relocations—and did not raise a separate tablet in each place.

sentences.zh: 議者或云：'東都神主，已曾虔奉而禮之，豈可以一朝廢之乎？

translations.literal: Some debaters said: "The Eastern Capital tablets were once reverently served and honored—how can they be cast aside in a single day?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said the eastern tablets had been reverently served—could they be cast aside in a day?

sentences.zh: '且虞祭則立桑主而虔祀，練祭則立栗主而埋桑主，豈桑主不曾虔祀，而乃埋之？

translations.literal: "At yu sacrifice the mulberry tablet is erected and reverently offered; at lian sacrifice the chestnut tablet is erected and the mulberry buried—was the mulberry never reverently offered, yet buried?"
translations.idiomatic: At yu you erect and worship the mulberry tablet; at lian you raise chestnut and bury mulberry—had mulberry never been worshipped before burial?

sentences.zh: 又所闕之主，不可更作，作之不時，非禮也。」

translations.literal: "Moreover the missing tablets cannot be remade; remaking them out of season is uncanonical." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Nor could lost tablets be replaced untimely—remaking off-season was uncanonical. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 長慶元年二月，分司官庫部員外郎李渤奏：「太微宮神主，請歸祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Changqing, Li Bo, Outer-Assignment Vice Director of the Storehouse Bureau, memorialized: "The spirit tablets in Taiwei Palace should be returned for enshrinement in the Grand Temple."
translations.idiomatic: Changqing 1, second month: Li Bo, eastern-capital Storehouse vice director, asked to reunite Taiwei Palace tablets with the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 」敕付東都留守鄭絪商量聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict referred the matter to Eastern Capital Regent Zheng Yin for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: The edict referred the matter to regent Zheng Yin at the eastern capital for deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: '絪奏云：「臣謹詳三代典禮，上稽高祖、太宗之制度，未嘗有並建兩朝、並饗二主之禮。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized: "Your servant has examined the rites of the Three Dynasties and traced Gaozu and Taizong's institutions—never was there a rite of founding two halls in tandem or feasting two sets of tablets together."
translations.idiomatic: Yin reported: he had traced Three Dynasties ritual and Gaozu and Taizong's institutions—never two halls built in parallel or two tablet lines feasted together.

sentences.zh: 天授之際，祀典變革。

translations.literal: During the Tian-shou reign the sacrificial code was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: At Tian-shou the sacrificial code shifted.

sentences.zh: 中宗初復舊物，未暇詳考典章，遂於洛陽創宗廟。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong first restored former things he had no time to scrutinize the canon and founded an ancestral shrine at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong, restoring the old order in haste, never examined the classics and raised a lineage temple at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是行遷都之制，實非建國之儀。

translations.literal: That followed the protocol of moving the capital, not the ceremony of founding the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It matched removal of seat, not founding of state.

sentences.zh: 及西歸上都，因循未廢。

translations.literal: Once the court returned west to the Upper Capital, inertia left the practice standing.
translations.idiomatic: After returning west to the principal capital, inertia left it standing.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣統，墜典克修，東都九廟，不復告饗。

translations.literal: Dezong succeeded and restored fallen rites; the nine shrines of the Eastern Capital ceased to receive sacrificial announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, fallen observance was repaired and the eastern nine halls ceased to receive sacrificial announcement.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮記》，仲尼答曾子問曰：'天無二日，土無二王，嘗、禘、郊、社，尊無二上。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Rites, when Zengzi asked, Confucius answered: "Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings—in seasonal, great, suburban, and soil rites, honor has no second apex."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites records Confucius telling Zengzi: heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings—in seasonal, great, suburban, and soil rites, honor has no second apex.

sentences.zh: '所以明二主之非禮也。

translations.literal: Thus he showed that two sets of spirit tablets violated ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thus two tablet-halls were uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 陛下接千載之大統，揚累聖之耿光，憲章先王，垂法後嗣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received the great succession of a thousand years, raising the bright glory of successive sages, taking the constitution of former kings as model and statute for generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds a thousand-year succession, lifts the bright glory of successive sages, takes former kings as model, and sets law for those who follow.

sentences.zh: 況宗廟之禮，至尊至重，違經黷祀，時謂不欽。

translations.literal: Ancestral-hall rites are of utmost dignity and weight—defying the classics in careless sacrifice the age calls impiety.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral rites are weightiest of all—defying the canon in sacrifice the age calls impiety.

sentences.zh: 特望擇三代令典，守高祖、太宗之憲度，鑒神龍權宜之制，遵建中矯正之禮，依經復古，允屬聖明。

translations.literal: I beg that you choose the excellent canon of the Three Dynasties, keep Gaozu and Taizong's fundamental law, reflect on the Shenlong expedient, follow Jianzhong's corrective rite, and restore antiquity by the classics—befitting such sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the Three Dynasties' best canon, keep Gaozu and Taizong's law, read Shenlong's expedient and Jianzhong's correction, restore antiquity by the classics—befitting such sagacity.

sentences.zh: 伏乙太微宮光皇帝三代、睿宗聖文孝武皇帝神主，參考經義，不合祔饗。

translations.literal: I submit that the Taiwei Palace tablets of Emperor Guang for three generations and Emperor Ruizong the Sagely Literary Filial Martial, weighed against the classics, ought not be affixed for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiwei tablets of Emperor Guang (three generations) and Ruizong the Sagely Literary Filial Martial, weighed against the classics, should not be affixed for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 至於遷置神主之禮，三代以降，經無明文。

translations.literal: As for rites of moving and setting tablets, since the Three Dynasties the classics give no explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for moving and setting tablets have no explicit classic text since the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 伏望委中書門下與公卿禮官質正詳定。

translations.literal: I beg that the Secretariat-Chancellery with dukes, ministers, and ritual officers verify and fix the matter in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the Secretariat-Chancellery, dukes, and ritual officers to verify and fix the matter.

sentences.zh: 」敕付所司。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the responsible offices. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The edict assigned it to the proper bureaus. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 太常博士王彥威等奏議曰：

translations.literal: Supervisor of Sacrifices Wang Yanwei and others submitted a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ritual director Wang Yanwei and colleagues deliberated:

sentences.zh: 謹按國初故事，無兩都並建宗廟、並行饗祭之禮。

translations.literal: According to founding precedent, there was no rite of building ancestral shrines in both capitals and conducting sacrifice in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Founding precedent knew no parallel shrines in both capitals or parallel feast lines.

sentences.zh: 伏尋《周書》、《召誥》、《洛誥》之說，實有祭告豐廟、洛廟之文，是則周人兩都並建宗祧，至則告饗。

translations.literal: Searching the Documents of Zhou, Announcement to Shao, and Announcement concerning Luo, there are texts of sacrifice and announcement at the Feng and Luo shrines—the Zhou in both seats built lineage temples and, when they arrived, announced sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Documents, Announcement to Shao, and Luo Announcement record sacrifice at Feng and Luo—the Zhou built lineage temples in both seats and announced feast when they arrived.

sentences.zh: 然則兩都皆祭祖考，禮祀並興。

translations.literal: Thus both capitals sacrificed to fathers and grandfathers; ritual observance rose in both.
translations.idiomatic: Both capitals sacrificed to fathers and grandfathers; ritual rose in both.

sentences.zh: 自神龍復辟，中宗嗣位，廟既偕作，饗亦並行。

translations.literal: From Shenlong restoration and Zhongzong's succession, shrines were built together and feasts ran in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: From Shenlong restoration and Zhongzong's succession, shrines were built together and feasts ran in parallel

sentences.zh: 天寶末，兩都傾陷，神主亡失。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao both capitals fell; spirit tablets were lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao both capitals fell.

sentences.zh: 肅宗既復舊物，但建廟作主於上都。

translations.literal: Once Suzong restored former goods, he only built shrines and made tablets in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong restored what was lost but built shrines and tablets only in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 其東都神主，大曆中始於人間得之，遂寓於太微宮，不復祔饗。

translations.literal: The eastern tablets were recovered among the people only in the Dali era and lodged in Taiwei Palace, never again affixed for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern tablets surfaced among the people only in Dali, lodged in Taiwei Palace, never again affixed for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹按經傳，王者之制，凡建居室，宗廟為先，廟必有主，主必在廟。

translations.literal: We examine the classics and commentaries: the king's rule—whenever dwellings are built, ancestral shrines come first; a shrine must have tablets, tablets must be in the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Classics say: when a king builds dwellings, ancestral shrines come first; a shrine must have tablets, tablets must dwell in the shrine.

sentences.zh: 是則立廟兩都，蓋行古之道，主必在廟，實依禮經。

translations.literal: Thus to raise shrines in both seats follows the ancient way; tablets must dwell in shrine—truly per the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines in both seats follow the ancient way; tablets in shrine follow the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 今謹參詳，理合升祔。

translations.literal: We now compare in detail: reason requires elevating them for enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: On full comparison, reason requires elevating them for enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 謹按光皇帝是追王，高宗、中宗、睿宗是祧廟之主，其神主合藏於太廟從西第一夾室。

translations.literal: Emperor Guang was a posthumous ennoblement; Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong are diao-shrine lords—their tablets should be stored in the Grand Temple's first western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guang was posthumously ennobled; Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong are diao-shrine lords—their tablets belong in the Grand Temple's first western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝是始封不遷之祖，其神主合藏於太廟從西第一室。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing was the founder enfeoffed, never displaced—his tablet should be stored in the Grand Temple's first western main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing was the founder enfeoffed, never displaced—his tablet belongs in the first western main chamber.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太宗、玄宗、肅宗、代宗是創業有功親廟之祖。

translations.literal: Gaozu, Taizong, Xuanzong, Suzong, and Daizong were close-shrine ancestors who founded the enterprise with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, Taizong, Xuanzong, Suzong, and Daizong were close-shrine ancestors who founded the enterprise with merit

sentences.zh: 伏准《江都集禮》：'正廟之主，藏於太室之中。

translations.literal: Per the Jiangdu Collected Rites: "The principal shrine's tablets are stored within the Grand Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdu Collected Rites: principal shrine tablets are stored in the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: '《禮記》：'君廟之主，有故則聚而藏諸祖廟。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites: "When a ruler's shrine tablets have cause, they are gathered and stored in the ancestral shrine."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites: when a ruler's shrine tablets have cause, gather and store them in the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: '伏以德宗之下，神主未作，代宗之上，後主先亡，若歸本室，有虛神主。

translations.literal: We note: below Dezong no tablets were made; above Daizong later tablets perished first—if returned to original chambers, some seats would lack tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Below Dezong no tablets were made; above Daizong later tablets perished—return to original chambers and some seats stand empty.

sentences.zh: 事雖可據，理或未安。

translations.literal: The facts can be cited, yet the principle may not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Facts can be cited; principle may not yet be settled.

sentences.zh: 今高祖已下神主，併合藏于太祖之廟，依舊准故事不饗。

translations.literal: Now tablets from Gaozu downward should all be stored in the shrine of the Great Ancestor, per old precedent without sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets from Gaozu downward should all be stored in the Great Ancestor's shrine, per old precedent without sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 如陛下肆覲東後，移幸洛陽，自非祧主，合歸本室。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty tours the eastern regions and visits Luoyang, except diao lords, tablets should return to original chambers.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty tours east and visits Luoyang, except diao lords, tablets should return to their chambers.

sentences.zh: 其餘闕主，又當特作，而祔饗時祭、禘、祫如儀。

translations.literal: Other missing tablets must be specially made, and affixed sacrifice—seasonal, di, xia—as ritual requires.
translations.idiomatic: Other missing tablets must be specially made; affixed sacrifice—seasonal, di, xia—as ritual requires.

sentences.zh: 臣又按國家追王故事，太祖之上，又有德明、興聖、懿祖別廟。

translations.literal: We further note state precedent for posthumous kings: above the Great Ancestor are separate shrines to Deming, Xingsheng, and Yizu.
translations.idiomatic: State precedent for posthumous kings places separate shrines above the Great Ancestor—to Deming, Xingsheng, and Yizu.

sentences.zh: 今光皇帝神主，即懿祖也。

translations.literal: The present Emperor Guang's tablet is Yizu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guang's tablet is Yizu.

sentences.zh: 伏緣東都先無前件廟宇，光皇帝神主今請權祔於太廟夾室，居元皇帝之上。

translations.literal: Because the eastern capital previously lacked those shrines, Emperor Guang's tablet is now provisionally affixed in the Grand Temple side chamber, above Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital lacked those shrines; Emperor Guang's tablet is provisionally affixed in the Grand Temple side chamber, above Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 如駕在東都，即請准上都式營建別廟，作德明、興聖、獻祖神主，備禮升祔。

translations.literal: If the throne is at the eastern capital, build separate shrines as in the Upper Capital, make tablets for Deming, Xingsheng, and Xianzu, and enshrine with full rite.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne is at the eastern capital, build separate shrines as in the Upper Capital, make tablets for Deming, Xingsheng, and Xianzu, and enshrine with full rite

sentences.zh: 又於太廟夾室奉迎光皇帝神主歸別廟第四室，禘、祫如儀。

translations.literal: Also from the Grand Temple side chamber escort Emperor Guang's tablet to the fourth chamber of the separate shrine, di and xia as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Also escort Emperor Guang's tablet from the side chamber to the fourth chamber of the separate shrine, di and xia as ritual.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「禮，作栗主，瘞桑主。

translations.literal: Someone asked: "The rites say make the chestnut tablet and bury the mulberry tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: the rites say make the chestnut tablet and bury the mulberry tablet.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏並有瘞桑之議，大曆中亦瘞孝敬皇帝神主，今祔而不瘞，如之何？

translations.literal: Han and Wei both debated burying mulberry; in Dali they buried Filial Emperor Xiaojing's tablet—now affix without burying, how so? The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei debated burying mulberry; in Dali they buried Filial Emperor Xiaojing's tablet—now affix without burying, how so? The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「作主依神，理無可埋，漢魏瘞藏，事非允愜。

translations.literal: Answer: "Tablets embody the spirit—by principle nothing to bury; Han-Wei burial storage was not truly fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Answer: tablets embody the spirit—by principle nothing to bury; Han-Wei burial storage was not truly fitting.

sentences.zh: 孝敬尊非正統，廟廢而主獨存，從而瘞藏，為葉情理。」

translations.literal: "Filial Xiaojing was not orthodox lineage; his shrine was abandoned while his tablet alone survived—burying it followed abandoned reason." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Filial Xiaojing was not orthodox lineage; his shrine was abandoned while his tablet alone survived—burying it followed abandoned reason. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 又問：「古者巡狩，必載遷主，今東都主又祔於廟。

translations.literal: Again asked: "In antiquity on tour one carried the displacement tablet; now eastern tablets are also affixed in the shrine."
translations.idiomatic: Again asked: in antiquity on tour one carried the displacement tablet; now eastern tablets are also affixed in the shrine.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「古者師行以遷主，無則主命，自非遷祖之主，別無出廟之文。

translations.literal: Answer: "In antiquity armies marched with displacement tablets; without them, tablets commanded—except displacement ancestors' tablets, no canon text for removing tablets from shrine."
translations.idiomatic: Answer: in antiquity armies marched with displacement tablets; without them, tablets commanded—except displacement ancestors' tablets, no canon text for removing tablets from shrine.

sentences.zh: 凡邑有宗廟先君之主曰都，則兩都宗廟，各宜有主。」

translations.literal: "Any settlement with ancestral shrines and former lords' tablets is called a capital—thus both capitals' shrines should each have tablets." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Any settlement with ancestral shrines and former lords' tablets is a capital—both capitals' shrines should each have tablets. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「古者作主，必因虞、練，若主必歸祔，則室不可虛，則當補已亡之主，創當祔之主。

translations.literal: Asked again: "In antiquity making tablets required yu and lian; if tablets must return for enshrinement, chambers cannot stand empty—one must replace lost tablets and create those due for enshrinement."
translations.idiomatic: Asked again: in antiquity making tablets required yu and lian; if tablets must return for enshrinement, chambers cannot stand empty—replace lost tablets and create those due for enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 禮經無說，如之何？

translations.literal: The ritual classics say nothing—what then? The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual classics say nothing—what then? The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「虞、練作主，禮之正也。

translations.literal: Answer: "Yu and lian tablet-making is ritual's proper way."
translations.idiomatic: Answer: yu and lian tablet-making is ritual's proper way.

sentences.zh: 非時作主，事之權也。

translations.literal: Off-season tablet-making is expedient for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Off-season tablet-making is expedient for the moment

sentences.zh: 王者遭時為法，因事制宜，苟無其常，則思其變。

translations.literal: A king meets the age with law, shapes affairs to need—if the constant is absent, consider variation.
translations.idiomatic: A king meets the age with law, shapes affairs to need—if the constant is absent, consider variation

sentences.zh: 如駕或東幸，廟仍虛主，即准肅宗廣德二年上都作主故事，特作闕主而祔。

translations.literal: If the throne tours east while the shrine still lacks tablets, follow Suzong's Guangde 2 precedent of making tablets at the Upper Capital—specially make missing tablets and enshrine.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne tours east while the shrine still lacks tablets, follow Suzong's Guangde 2 precedent—specially make missing tablets and enshrine.

sentences.zh: 蓋主不可闕，故禮貴從宜，《春秋》之義，變而正之者。

translations.literal: "For tablets cannot be wanting, ritual esteems fitting expedient—the Spring and Autumn principle is to vary and thereby rectify." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets cannot be wanting, so ritual esteems fitting expedient—the Spring and Autumn principle is to vary and thereby rectify. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」臣伏思祖宗之主，神靈所憑，寓於太微，不入宗廟，據經復本，允屬聖明。

translations.literal: We reflect: ancestors' tablets, where spirits dwell, lodged in Taiwei not entering the lineage shrine—restoring root by the classics befits sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors' tablets, where spirits dwell, lodged in Taiwei not entering the lineage shrine—restoring root by the classics befits sagacity.

sentences.zh: 至是下尚書省集議，而郎吏所議，與彥威多同。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat was ordered to convene deliberation; expectant officials' views largely agreed with Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was ordered to convene; expectant officials largely agreed with Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 丞郎則各執所見，或曰「神主合藏于太微宮；

translations.literal: Directors and vice-directors each held their view: some said "tablets should be stored in Taiwei Palace";
translations.idiomatic: Directors and vice-directors each held their view: some said tablets should be stored in Taiwei Palace;

sentences.zh: 」或云「併合埋瘞」；

translations.literal: some said "bury them together";
translations.idiomatic: some said bury them together;

sentences.zh: 或云「闕主當作」；

translations.literal: some said "missing tablets should be made";
translations.idiomatic: some said missing tablets should be made;

sentences.zh: 或云「輿駕東幸，即載上都神主而東」。

translations.literal: some said "when the carriage tours east, carry Upper Capital tablets east."
translations.idiomatic: some said when the carriage tours east, carry Upper Capital tablets east.

sentences.zh: 鹹以意言，不本經據。

translations.literal: All spoke from opinion, not grounded in canonical evidence.
translations.idiomatic: All spoke from opinion, not grounded in canonical evidence

sentences.zh: 竟以紛議不定，遂不舉行。

translations.literal: In the end confused debate brought no decision and nothing was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Confused debate brought no decision; nothing was carried out.

sentences.zh: 會昌五年八月，中書門下奏：「東都太廟九室神主，共二十六座，自祿山叛後，取太廟為軍營，神主棄於街巷，所司潛收聚，見在太微宮內新造小屋之內。

translations.literal: Huichang 5, eighth month: Secretariat-Chancellery reported that the Eastern Capital Grand Temple's nine chambers held twenty-six spirit tablets; after An Lushan's rebellion the temple became barracks and tablets were cast into streets—the offices secretly gathered them and they now rest in a new small building inside Taiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang 5, eighth month: the Secretariat reported the Eastern Capital Grand Temple's nine chambers held twenty-six tablets; after An Lushan's rebellion the temple became barracks and tablets were cast into streets—the offices secretly gathered them; they now rest in a new small building inside Taiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: 其太廟屋室並在，可以修崇。

translations.literal: The Grand Temple buildings remain and can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The temple buildings still stood and could be restored.

sentences.zh: 大和中，太常博士議，以為東都不合置神主，車駕東幸，即載主而行。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era ritual directors held the eastern capital should not hold tablets—when the throne toured east, carry tablets along.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe, ritual directors held the eastern capital should not hold tablets—when the throne toured east, carry tablets along.

sentences.zh: 至今因循，尚未修建。

translations.literal: To this day inertia has left restoration undone.
translations.idiomatic: Inertia has left restoration undone to this day.

sentences.zh: 望令尚書省集公卿及禮官、學官詳議。

translations.literal: We ask that the Secretariat gather dukes, ritual officers, and academicians for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: They asked the Secretariat to gather dukes, ritual officers, and academicians for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 如不要更置，須有收藏去處。

translations.literal: If they are not to be set up anew, there must be a place to store them.
translations.idiomatic: If tablets were not to be reinstalled, a proper storehouse was needed.

sentences.zh: 如合置，望以所拆大寺材木修建。

translations.literal: If they should be installed, we ask to rebuild using timber from dismantled great temples.
translations.idiomatic: If they should be installed, rebuild using timber from dismantled great temples.

sentences.zh: 既是宗室官居守，便望令充修東都太廟使，勾當修繕。

translations.literal: Since a member of the imperial clan holds the post of eastern-resident commissioner, it is requested he be appointed Commissioner for Rebuilding the Eastern Capital Grand Temple to oversee repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because a prince held the eastern residency, he should be named commissioner to rebuild the Grand Temple and supervise repairs.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕宜依。

translations.literal: Approved as ordered. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Approved as ordered. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 六年三月，太常博士鄭路等奏：「東都太微宮神主二十座，去年二月二十九日禮院分析聞奏訖。

translations.literal: Sixth year, third month: ritual director Zheng Lu and others reported that twenty tablets in Taiwei Palace at the eastern capital had been analyzed by the Ritual Office and reported on the twenty-ninth day of the second month last year.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6, third month: ritual director Zheng Lu reported twenty Taiwei Palace tablets; the Ritual Office had analyzed and reported them on the twenty-ninth of the second month last year.

sentences.zh: 伏奉今月七日敕，'此禮至重，須遵典故，宜令禮官、學官同議聞奏'者。

translations.literal: We received this month's seventh-day edict: "This rite is weightiest; precedent must be followed—ritual and academic officers should deliberate together and report."
translations.idiomatic: They received this month's seventh-day edict: this rite is weightiest; precedent must be followed—ritual and academic officers should deliberate together and report.

sentences.zh: 臣今與學官等詳議訖，謹具分析如後：獻祖宣皇帝、宣莊皇后、懿祖光皇帝、光懿皇后、文德皇后、高宗天皇大帝、則天皇后、中宗大聖大昭孝皇帝、和思皇后、昭成皇后、孝敬皇帝、地敬哀皇后已前十二座，親盡迭毀，宜遷諸太廟，祔於興聖廟。

translations.literal: We have deliberated with academicians and submit analysis: the twelve tablets before—Xianzu Emperor Xuan, Empress Xuanzhuang, Yizu Emperor Guang, Empress Guangyi, Empress Wende, Emperor Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great, Empress Wu Zetian, Emperor Zhongzong the Great Sage Great Filial, Empress Hespi, Empress Zhaocheng, Emperor Xiaojing, Empress Di'ai—whose kin is exhausted and rotation destroyed, should move to line shrines and affix at Xingsheng Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberating with academicians, they submitted analysis: twelve tablets—Xianzu Emperor Xuan, Empress Xuanzhuang, Yizu Emperor Guang, Empress Guangyi, Empress Wende, Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great, Empress Wu Zetian, Zhongzong the Great Sage Great Filial, Empress Hespi, Empress Zhaocheng, Emperor Xiaojing, Empress Di'ai—whose kin is exhausted, should move to line shrines and affix at Xingsheng Shrine.

sentences.zh: 禘祫之歲，乃一祭之。

translations.literal: In years of di-xia, they receive one sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In di-xia years they receive one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 東都無興聖廟可祔，伏請且權藏於太廟夾室。

translations.literal: The eastern capital has no Xingsheng Shrine for enshrinement—we beg provisional storage in the Grand Temple side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital has no Xingsheng Shrine—we beg provisional storage in the Grand Temple side chamber.

sentences.zh: 未題神主十四座，前件神主既無題號之文，難伸祝告之禮。

translations.literal: Fourteen tablets bear no inscription; without inscription text, invocation and announcement cannot proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen tablets bear no inscription; without inscription, invocation and announcement cannot proceed.

sentences.zh: 今與禮官等商量，伏請告遷之日，但瘞於舊太微宮內空閒之地。

translations.literal: Deliberating with ritual officers, we beg that on the day of removal announcement they be buried only in vacant ground within the old Taiwei Palace. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberating with ritual officers, they begged that on removal day the tablets be buried in vacant ground within the old Taiwei Palace. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 恭酌事理，庶協從宜。

translations.literal: Respectfully weighing the matter, it should accord with convenience.
translations.idiomatic: That, they judged, best fit practical need.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: Approved. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Approved. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 太常博士段瑰等三十九人奏議曰：

translations.literal: Thirty-nine ritual directors including Duan Gui submitted a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-nine ritual directors including Duan Gui submitted a deliberation:

sentences.zh: 禮之所立，本於誠敬；

translations.literal: What ritual establishes rests on sincerity and reverence;
translations.idiomatic: What ritual establishes rests on sincerity and reverence

sentences.zh: 廟之所設，實在尊嚴。

translations.literal: what shrines establish is truly dignity.
translations.idiomatic: what shrines establish is truly dignity

sentences.zh: 既曰薦誠，則宜統一。

translations.literal: Since it is offering sincerity, unity is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Since sacrifice is sincerity offered, unity is fitting.

sentences.zh: 昔周之東西有廟，亦可征其所由。

translations.literal: When Zhou had eastern and western shrines, one can trace why.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou had eastern and western shrines, one can trace why

sentences.zh: 但緣卜洛之初，既須營建，又以遷都未決，因議兩留。

translations.literal: Only at the first divination for Luo building was needed, and removal of seat unsettled, hence deliberation to keep both.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the first divination for Luo, building was needed and the seat unsettled—hence deliberation to keep both.

sentences.zh: 酌其事情，匪務於廣，祭法明矣。

translations.literal: Weighing circumstances, not aiming at breadth—the Sacrificial Canon is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing circumstances, not aiming at breadth—the Sacrificial Canon is clear

sentences.zh: 伏以東都太廟，廢已多時，若議增修，稍乖前訓。

translations.literal: The eastern Grand Temple has long lain abandoned—if we debate restoration, it slightly strays from prior teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Grand Temple has long lain abandoned—debating restoration slightly strays from prior teaching.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why (idiomatic).

sentences.zh: 東都始制寢廟於天后、中宗之朝，事出一時，非貞觀、開元之法，前後因循不廢者，亦踵鎬京之文也。

translations.literal: The eastern shrine was first made in Empress Wu and Zhongzong's reign—a moment's affair, not Zhenguan or Kaiyuan law; what lingered unrepealed merely followed Haojing's text.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern shrine was first made under Empress Wu and Zhongzong—a moment's affair, not Zhenguan or Kaiyuan law; what lingered unrepealed merely followed Haojing's precedent.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「祭不欲數，數則煩。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Sacrifice should not be frequent—frequency breeds weariness."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: sacrifice should not be frequent—frequency breeds weariness.

sentences.zh: 」天寶之中，兩京悉為寇陷，西都廟貌如故，東都因此散亡。

translations.literal: In Tianbao both capitals fell to rebels; the western capital's shrine façades remained, the eastern thus scattered. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao both capitals fell to rebels; the western shrine façades remained, the eastern scattered. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 是知九廟之靈，不欲歆其煩祀也。

translations.literal: Thus the nine shrines' spirits did not wish to inhale wearisome sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the nine shrines' spirits did not wish to inhale wearisome sacrifice

sentences.zh: 自建中不葺之後，彌曆歲年。

translations.literal: From Jianzhong's refusal to repair, years have piled.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianzhong's refusal to repair, years have piled

sentences.zh: 今若廟貌惟新，即須室別有主。

translations.literal: If shrine façades are renewed today, each chamber must have its tablet.
translations.idiomatic: If shrine façades are renewed today, each chamber must have its tablet

sentences.zh: 舊主雖在，大半合祧，必几筵而存之，所謂宜祧不祧也。

translations.literal: Old tablets remain but most should merge in diao—yet they must be kept on spirit benches—what should diao not diao.
translations.idiomatic: Old tablets remain but most should merge in diao—yet kept on spirit benches—what should diao not diao.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，「當七廟五廟，無虛主也」，謂廟不得無主者也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "When there are seven or five shrines, no empty tablet"—meaning shrines cannot lack tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, when there are seven or five shrines, no empty tablet—meaning shrines cannot lack tablets.

sentences.zh: 舊主如有留去，新廟便合創添。

translations.literal: If old tablets remain or depart, the new shrine must add new ones.
translations.idiomatic: If old tablets remain or depart, the new shrine must add new ones

sentences.zh: 謹按《左傳》云：「祔練作主。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "Affix at lian, make tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: affix at lian, make tablet.

sentences.zh: 」又戴聖云：「虞而立几筵。

translations.literal: Dai Sheng says: "At yu, set the spirit bench."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sheng says: at yu, set the spirit bench.

sentences.zh: 」如或過時成之，便是以凶幹吉。

translations.literal: If made out of season, that is using the inauspicious to intrude on the auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If made out of season, that is using the inauspicious to intrude on the auspicious

sentences.zh: 創添既不典，虛廟又非儀。

translations.literal: Adding anew is uncanonical; empty shrine is unritual.
translations.idiomatic: Adding anew is uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 考諸禮文，進退無守。

translations.literal: Examining ritual texts, advance and retreat have no footing.
translations.idiomatic: Examining ritual texts, advance and retreat have no footing

sentences.zh: 或曰「漢于郡國置宗廟凡百餘所，今止東西立廟，有何不安」者。

translations.literal: Some say: "Han placed lineage shrines in commanderies and kingdoms, over a hundred—now only east and west shrines, what unease?" The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Some say: Han placed lineage shrines in commanderies and kingdoms, over a hundred—now only east and west shrines, what unease? The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 當漢氏承秦焚燒之餘，不識典故，至於廟制，率意而行。

translations.literal: When Han inherited Qin's burnings, it knew no canonical precedents—for shrine system, it acted by whim.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited Qin's burnings and knew no canonical precedents—for shrine system, it acted by whim.

sentences.zh: 比及元、成二帝之間，貢禹、韋玄成等繼出，果有正論，竟從毀除。

translations.literal: By Yuandi and Chengdi's reign Gong Yu, Wei Xuancheng and others appeared in succession with sound argument—finally shrines were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuandi and Chengdi, Gong Yu, Wei Xuancheng, and others argued soundly—finally shrines were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 足知漢初不本於禮經，又安可程法也？

translations.literal: Enough to know early Han did not root in ritual classics—how take it as measure?
translations.idiomatic: Enough to know early Han did not root in ritual classics—how take it as measure (idiomatic).

sentences.zh: 或曰「几筵不得復設，廟寢何妨修營，侯車駕時巡，便合於所載之主」者。

translations.literal: Some say: "Spirit benches cannot be reset—why not repair shrine chambers? When the carriage tours, use the tablets carried." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Some say: spirit benches cannot be reset—why not repair shrine chambers? When the carriage tours, use the tablets carried. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 究其終始，又得以論之。

translations.literal: Pursue beginning and end—again one may argue.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue beginning and end—again one may argue

sentences.zh: 昨者降敕參詳，本為欲收舊主，主既不立，廟何可施？

translations.literal: Yesterday's edict for deliberation aimed to gather old tablets—if tablets are not installed, how apply the shrine?
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday's edict aimed to gather old tablets—if tablets are not installed, how apply the shrine?

sentences.zh: 假令行幸九州；

translations.literal: Suppose the throne tours the nine provinces—
translations.idiomatic: Suppose throne tours nine provinces—

sentences.zh: 一一皆立廟乎」愚以為廟不可修，主宜藏瘞，或就瘞於坎室，或瘞於兩階間，此乃百代常行不易之道也。

translations.literal: must one raise a shrine in each? This servant holds: shrine cannot be repaired; tablets should be stored and buried—either in the pit chamber or between the two stair flights—the immutable way of a hundred generations. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: must one raise a shrine in each? This servant holds: the shrine cannot be repaired; tablets should be stored and buried—in the pit chamber or between the two stair flights—the immutable way of a hundred generations. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 其年九月敕：「段瑰等詳議，東都不可立廟。

translations.literal: That year, ninth month edict: "Duan Gui and others' deliberation—eastern capital cannot raise shrine."
translations.idiomatic: That year, ninth month edict: Duan Gui and others' deliberation—the eastern capital cannot raise a shrine.

sentences.zh: 李福等別狀，又有異同。

translations.literal: Li Fu and others' separate memorial also differs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu and others' separate memorial also differs

sentences.zh: 國家制度，須合典禮，證據未一，則難建立。

translations.literal: State institutions must match canonical rites—evidence not unified, then hard to establish.
translations.idiomatic: State institutions must match canonical rites—evidence not unified, then hard to establish

sentences.zh: 宜並令赴都省對議，須歸至當。」

translations.literal: All should come to the Secretariat for face debate until the fitting conclusion. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: All should come to the Secretariat for face debate until the fitting conclusion. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 工部尚書薛元賞等議：

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xue Yuanshang and others deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xue Yuanshang and others replied:

sentences.zh: 伏以建中時，公卿奏請修建東都慶廟，當時之議，大旨有三：其一曰，必存其廟，備立其主，時饗之日，以他官攝行。

translations.literal: At Jianzhong, dukes and ministers petitioned to restore the eastern celebratory shrine—then debate had three heads: first, keep the shrine, fully install tablets, on feast days have another officer perform by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianzhong, dukes petitioned to restore the eastern celebratory shrine—debate then had three heads: first, keep the shrine, fully install tablets, on feast days have another officer perform by proxy.

sentences.zh: 二曰，建廟立主，存而不祭，皇輿時巡，則就饗焉。

translations.literal: Second, build shrine and tablets, keep without sacrifice—when the imperial carriage tours, feast there.
translations.idiomatic: Second, build shrine and tablets, keep without sacrifice—when the imperial carriage tours, feast there

sentences.zh: 三曰，存其廟，一瘞其主。

translations.literal: Third, keep the shrine, bury the tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Third, keep shrine, bury tablets.

sentences.zh: 臣等立其三議，參酌禮經，理宜存廟，不合置主。

translations.literal: We set forth the three deliberations, weighing the ritual canon—reason requires keeping the shrine, not installing tablets.
translations.idiomatic: They set forth the three deliberations, weighing the ritual canon—reason requires keeping the shrine, not installing tablets.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮祭義》曰：「建國之神位，右社稷而左宗廟。

translations.literal: The Meaning of Sacrifice says: "In founding a state, spirit seats—sacred soil right, ancestral shrine left."
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Sacrifice says: in founding a state, spirit seats—sacred soil right, ancestral shrine left.

sentences.zh: 」《禮記》云：「君子將營宮室，宗廟為先。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites: "When the noble will build chambers, ancestral shrine comes first."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites: when the noble will build chambers, ancestral shrine comes first.

sentences.zh: 」是知王者建邦設都，必先宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: Thus the king founding realm and seat must first ancestral shrine and sacred soil.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the king founding realm and seat must first raise ancestral shrine and sacred soil.

sentences.zh: 況周武受命，始都于豐，成王相宅，又卜於洛，烝祭歲於新邑，冊周公於太室。

translations.literal: Zhou Wu received the mandate, first seat at Feng; Cheng Wang chose dwelling, divined again at Luo—sacrificed the year's harvest in the new settlement, enfeoffed Duke Zhou in the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wu received the mandate, first seat at Feng; Cheng Wang chose dwelling, divined at Luo—sacrificed the year's harvest in the new settlement, enfeoffed Duke Zhou in the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 故《書》曰：「戊辰，王在新邑，烝祭歲。

translations.literal: Thus the Documents: "On wuchen, the king in the new settlement sacrificed the year's harvest."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents: on wuchen, the king in the new settlement sacrificed the year's harvest.

sentences.zh: 王入太室祼。

translations.literal: The king entered the Grand Chamber for libation.
translations.idiomatic: king entered Grand Chamber for libation.

sentences.zh: 」成王厥後復立于豐，雖成洛邑，未嘗久處。

translations.literal: Cheng Wang afterward established again at Feng—though Luo was built, he did not long dwell there. The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wang afterward established again at Feng—though Luo was built, he did not long dwell there. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 逮于平王，始定東遷。

translations.literal: Reaching King Ping, eastern removal was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching King Ping, eastern removal was fixed

sentences.zh: 則周之豐、鎬，皆有宗廟明矣。

translations.literal: Then Zhou's Feng and Hao both had ancestral shrines—clear.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhou's Feng and Hao both had ancestral shrines—clear

sentences.zh: 又按，曾子問「廟有二主」，夫子對以「天無二日，土無二王，嘗、禘、郊、社，尊無二上，未知其為禮」者。

translations.literal: Also: Zengzi asked about "two tablet sets in the shrine"; the Master answered "Heaven no two suns, earth no two kings—in seasonal, great, suburban, soil rites, honor no second apex—unknown if that is ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Also: Zengzi asked about two tablet sets in the shrine; the Master answered heaven no two suns, earth no two kings—in seasonal, great, suburban, soil rites, honor no second apex—unknown if that is ritual.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公作二主，夫子譏之，以為偽主。

translations.literal: Once Duke Huan of Qi made two tablet sets; the Master mocked them as false tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi once made two tablet sets; the Master mocked them as false tablets.

sentences.zh: 是知二主不可並設，亦明矣。

translations.literal: Thus two tablet sets cannot be installed together—also clear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus two tablet sets cannot be installed together—also clear

sentences.zh: 夫聖王建社以厚本，立廟以尊祖，所以京邑必有宗社。

translations.idiomatic: With imperial dwelling established, spirit seats cannot stand empty—without ancestral shrine, what is imperial capital?

translations.idiomatic: Some cite the Rites: seven or five shrines, no empty tablet—meaning cannot lack tablets.

translations.literal: Your servant again probes ritual meaning and may discuss fully.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant again probes ritual meaning and may discuss fully

translations.literal: What is said—"no empty tablet"—means the shrine where sacrifice is seen cannot be empty.
translations.idiomatic: What is said—no empty tablet—means the shrine where sacrifice is seen cannot be empty.

translations.literal: Today's two capitals, though each has shrine—di, xia, feast, presentation—all are personally offered at the Upper Capital; tablet benches cannot stand empty in the eastern shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Today's two capitals, though each has a shrine—di, xia, feast, presentation—all are personally offered at the Upper Capital; tablet benches cannot stand empty in the eastern shrine.

sentences.zh: 且《禮》云：「唯聖人為能饗帝，孝子為能饗親。

translations.idiomatic: Two chambers do not dwell together—how can two shrines affix together (idiomatic).

translations.literal: Tablets for joint enshrinement, made untimely, were still mocked.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets for joint enshrinement, made untimely, were still mocked

sentences.zh: 今若置不合祔之主，不因時而作，違經越禮，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: Now to install tablets unfit for joint enshrinement, not made in season—defying canon, exceeding ritual—nothing worse.
translations.idiomatic: Now to install tablets unfit for joint enshrinement, not made in season—defying canon, exceeding ritual—nothing worse

translations.literal: How can there be tablets for nine chambers of joint feasting, yet text of installation without feasting?
translations.idiomatic: How can there be tablets for nine chambers of joint feasting.

translations.literal: Two shrines first created by Duke Zhou; two tablet sets mocked by the Master.
translations.idiomatic: Two shrines first created by Duke Zhou.

translations.literal: From antiquity creation has modeled Zhou and Confucius—old canon still remains, enough for clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity creation has modeled Zhou and Confucius—old canon still remains, enough for clear proof

sentences.zh: 臣所以言東都廟則合存，主不合置。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore says eastern shrine should be kept; tablets should not be installed.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant therefore says eastern shrine should be kept.

translations.literal: Now about to repair shrine buildings—truly no diminishment of canonical rite.
translations.idiomatic: Now about to repair shrine buildings—truly no diminishment of canonical rite

sentences.zh: 其見在太微宮中六主，請待東都建修太廟畢，具禮迎置於西夾室，閟而不饗，式彰陛下嚴祀之敬，以明聖朝尊祖之義。

translations.literal: The six tablets now in Taiwei—we ask after eastern Grand Temple repair is complete, with full rite escort them to the western side chamber, sealed without sacrifice, displaying Your Majesty's strict sacrificial reverence and clarifying the holy court's honor of ancestors.

translations.idiomatic: Ministry vice director Zheng Ya and five others: per the Ritual Office, the eastern Grand Temple abandoned cannot be restored; Taiwei tablets should be buried where they lodge.

translations.idiomatic: That strays from canonical teaching—they dare not echo it.

translations.literal: Your servant therefore filed a separate deliberation, asking repair and enshrinement of tablets, all per canonical rite—also the same as Rites Commissioner Yan Zhenqing's Jianzhong 1 memorial.
translations.idiomatic: They filed a separate deliberation, asking repair and enshrinement of tablets, all per canonical rite—also the same as Rites Commissioner Yan Zhenqing's Jianzhong 1 memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣與公卿等重議，皆以為廟固合修，主不可瘞，即與臣等別狀意同。

translations.literal: Deliberating again with dukes and ministers, all held shrine surely should be repaired, tablets cannot be buried—same as our separate memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberating again with dukes and ministers, all held the shrine surely should be repaired, tablets cannot be buried—same as their separate memorial.

translations.idiomatic: Yet collective debate still feared east and west shrines each setting tablets might touch two tablet sets in one shrine—request repair with empty chambers, store Taiwei tablets in side chambers.

translations.idiomatic: Six of those spirit-lords were unfilleted forebears; applying removal rites to them still seemed uncanonical.

translations.idiomatic: Imperial University director and Hongwen Guan attache Zheng Sui and seven others: in discussing the state's great affairs, one must root in rectitude and anchor in classics, to reach the middle way.

translations.literal: The sage dynasty takes broad filial piety first and obtaining the rites as precious—and how could ministers not answer with the classics?
translations.idiomatic: This dynasty prizes filial piety and true ritual—how could ministers answer with anything but the canon?

translations.literal: The three arguments and six antecedents have already been detailed in the prior deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Three positions and six precedents had already been laid out.

translations.literal: Again receiving heaven's inquiry, we set forth schools' views, seek in canonical instruction, examine the great mean—shrine has text requiring repair; tablet has no logic for installation.
translations.idiomatic: Again receiving heaven's inquiry, they set forth schools' views, sought canonical instruction, examined the great mean—shrine has text requiring repair; tablet has no logic for installation.

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: For what reason?

translations.literal: Orthodox classics and histories prove two-capital shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Orthodox classics and histories prove two-capital shrines

translations.literal: Then the theory of abandoning temples is perhaps not what should be abandoned.

translations.literal: We examine Poetry, Documents, Rites—the three classics and Han's two histories—both capitals set shrines; the institution of carrying tablets has long been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry, Documents, Rites—the three classics—and Han's two histories show both capitals set shrines; carrying tablets has long been practiced.

sentences.zh: 敢不明征而去文飾，援據經文，不易前見，東都太廟，合務修崇，而舊主當瘞，請于太微宮所藏之所。

translations.literal: How dare we leave clear proof for ornament? Citing classics, not changing prior views—the eastern Grand Temple should be repaired and honored; old tablets should be buried, we ask, where Taiwei stores them.

translations.literal: Although ritual arises from feeling, its aim is to clarify essentials; the true point is moderation—going beyond ritual in search of excess in fact diminishes sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual follows feeling but aims at essentials; moderation is the point—excess ritual undermines sincerity.

translations.idiomatic: They also say: "Though Zhenguan's founding left no leisure, how can this not be Kaiyuan law?"

translations.idiomatic: I cite the edict fixing the Kaiyuan Six Institutions: "In leisure from government, collating past and present, modeling the Zhou Offices, making the Tang Code."

translations.literal: Surveying its beginning and end—a thousand years in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying beginning and end—a thousand years in one morning.

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn calls this the method of examining antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn calls this the method of examining antiquity.

sentences.zh: 行之可久，不曰然歟？

translations.literal: That it may be practiced for long—is this not so?"
translations.idiomatic: That it may endure long—is this not so?"

translations.idiomatic: "Seven or five temples with no empty tablet"—yet they want empty temples—what canon allows this?

sentences.zh: 前稱廟貌如故者，即指建中之中，就有而言，以為國之先也。

translations.literal: The earlier statement that the temple appearance was as of old refers to the Jianzhong period, speaking of what existed then as the state's priority.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that temple buildings remain as of old refers to Jianzhong, when they still stood as the state's priority.

sentences.zh: 前以非時不造主者，謂見有神主，不得以非時而造也。

translations.literal: The earlier statement on not making tablets out of season means that where spirit tablets exist, one may not make them out of season.
translations.idiomatic: The claim against out-of-season tablet-making means existing tablets may not be remade out of season.

sentences.zh: 若江左至德之際，主並散亡，不可拘以例也。

translations.literal: If in the Jiangzuo period at the Zhide era tablets were all scattered and lost, one cannot be bound by that example.
translations.idiomatic: When tablets were all lost in the Jiangzuo Zhide era, that example cannot bind us.

sentences.zh: 或曰「廢主之瘞，請在太微宮」者。

translations.literal: Some say, "For burying abolished tablets, request the Taiwei Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Some propose burying abolished tablets in the Taiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: 謹按天寶二年敕曰：「古之制禮，祭用質明，義兼取于尚幽，情實緣於既沒。

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the Tianbao second-year edict: "Ancient ritual-making used plain dawn for sacrifice, meaning both drawing on what is remote and because feeling truly follows upon death.
translations.idiomatic: I cite Tianbao 2: ancient rites used plain dawn, drawing on remoteness because feeling follows death.

sentences.zh: 我聖祖澹然當在，為道之法，既殊有盡之期，宜展事生之禮。

translations.literal: Our sage ancestor calmly remains present; in the law of the Way, since there is no period of ending, it is fitting to extend the rites of honoring the living.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage ancestor remains present; in the Way there is no "ended" period—rites of honoring the living should extend.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，每至聖祖宮有昭告，宜改用卯時」者。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever there is announcement at the sage ancestor's palace, the mao hour should be used instead."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth announcements at the sage ancestor's palace should use the mao hour instead."

sentences.zh: 今欲以主瘞于宮所，即與此敕全乖。

translations.literal: Now to wish to bury tablets at the palace site is wholly at odds with this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Burying tablets at the palace site contradicts this edict entirely.

sentences.zh: 又曰：主不合瘞，請藏夾室」者。

translations.literal: Others say: tablets should not be buried—request storing them in side chambers."
translations.idiomatic: Others say tablets should not be buried but stored in side chambers.

sentences.zh: 謹按前代藏主，頗有異同。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that storing tablets in former ages had much variation.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages varied in storing tablets.

sentences.zh: 至如夾室，宜用以序昭穆也。

translations.literal: As for side chambers, they are properly used to order zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Side chambers properly order zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 今廟主俱不中禮，則無禘祫之文。

translations.literal: Now the temple tablets are all not in accord with ritual—then there is no text for di and xia.
translations.idiomatic: Present tablets are all ritually improper—there is no di/xia text.

sentences.zh: 又曰君子將營宮室，以宗廟為先，則建國營宮室而宗廟必設。

translations.literal: It also says that when the gentleman is about to build palaces, the ancestral temple comes first—then in founding a state and building palaces the temple must be set up.
translations.idiomatic: When building palaces the temple comes first—founding a state requires a temple.

sentences.zh: 東都既有宮室，而太廟不合不營。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital already has palaces—how can the Grand Temple not be built?
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital has palaces—the Grand Temple must not be left unbuilt.

sentences.zh: 凡以論之，其義斯勝。

translations.literal: Judging all arguments, this side prevails in principle.
translations.idiomatic: On the whole, this argument prevails.

sentences.zh: 而西周、東漢，並曰兩都，其各有宗廟之證，經史昭然，又得以極思於揚榷。

translations.literal: Yet Western Zhou and Eastern Han are both called two-capital states; that each had its own ancestral temple is clear in classics and histories—one may fully weigh the pros and cons.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhou and Eastern Han were both two-capital states; separate ancestral temples are plain in classics and histories—one may weigh the debate fully.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「其繩則直，縮板以載，作廟翼翼。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Its cord is straight; shrink the boards to load them—building the temple, majestic."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes: "Its cord is straight; shrink the boards—building the temple, majestic."

sentences.zh: 」《大雅》「瓜瓞」，言豐廟之作也。

translations.literal: " The Great Odes' "Melon Vine" speaks of building the Feng temple.
translations.idiomatic: The "Melon Vine" ode in the Great Odes describes building the Feng temple.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「于穆清廟，肅雍顯相。

translations.literal: It also says: "Solemn is the clear temple; dignified and manifest the assistants."
translations.idiomatic: Also: "Solemn is the clear temple; dignified, manifest assistants."

sentences.zh: 」洛邑既成，以率文王之祀。

translations.literal: " When Luoyang was complete, he led the sacrifices to King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was complete, he led sacrifices to King Wen.

sentences.zh: 此《詩》言洛之廟也。

translations.literal: This Ode speaks of Luoyang's temple.
translations.idiomatic: That ode is Luoyang's temple.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「成王既至洛，烝祭歲，文王騂牛一。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "When King Cheng reached Luo, he performed the year's zheng sacrifice—a red bull for King Wen."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents: "King Cheng reached Luo, performed the year's zheng sacrifice—a red bull for King Wen."

sentences.zh: 」又曰「裸於太室」，康王又居豐，「命畢公保厘東郊。

translations.literal: " It also says "libation in the Grand Chamber"; King Kang again dwelt at Feng—"he ordered Duke Bi to protect and govern the eastern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Also "libation in the Grand Chamber"; Kang dwelt at Feng—"ordered Duke Bi to protect the eastern suburb."

sentences.zh: 」豈 有無廟而可烝祭，非都而設保厘？

translations.literal: " How could there be zheng sacrifice without a temple, or setting protectorship without being the capital?
translations.idiomatic: How sacrifice without a temple, or a protectorship without a capital?

sentences.zh: 則《書》東西之廟也。

translations.literal: Thus the Documents shows temples east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Documents shows east-west temples.

sentences.zh: 逮于後漢卜洛，西京之廟亦存。

translations.literal: Down to Later Han's divination for Luo, the Western Capital's temples also remained.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han divined for Luo; Western Capital temples remained.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，於洛陽立廟，而成、哀、平三帝祭於西京。

translations.literal: In Jianwu year 2 a temple was built at Luoyang, while Cheng, Ai, and Ping were sacrificed to in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 2 built a Luoyang temple; Cheng, Ai, and Ping were sacrificed to in the west.

sentences.zh: 一十八年，親幸長安，行禘禮，當時五室列於洛都，三帝留於京廟，行幸之歲，與合食之期相會，不奉齋車，又安可以成此禮？

translations.literal: In year 18 the emperor personally visited Chang'an and performed the di rite; at the time five chambers stood in Luoyang, three emperors remained in the capital temple—when the imperial visit coincided with the joint feast, without bringing the fasting carriage, how could this rite be completed?
translations.idiomatic: Year 18 the emperor visited Chang'an for di; five chambers stood in Luoyang, three emperors in the capital temple—without the fasting carriage on a joint-feast year, how complete the rite?

sentences.zh: 則知兩廟周人成法，載主以行，漢家通制。

translations.literal: Thus one knows two temples were Zhou's established law; carrying tablets on tour was Han's regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Two temples were Zhou's law; carrying tablets on tour was Han's custom.

sentences.zh: 或以當虛一都之廟為不可，而引「七廟無虛主」之文。

translations.literal: Some take making one capital's temple empty as impossible and cite "seven temples must have no empty tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Some cite "no empty tablet" against emptying one capital's temple.

sentences.zh: 《禮》言一都之廟，室不虛主，非為兩都各廟而不可虛也。

translations.literal: The Ritual speaks of one capital's temples—chambers must not lack tablets—not that two capitals each with temples cannot be empty.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual means one capital's chambers must not lack tablets—not that two capitals cannot each have temples.

sentences.zh: 既聯出征之辭，更明載主之意，因事而言，理實相統，非如詩人更可斷章以取義也。

translations.literal: Having linked the language of the campaign, it further clarifies the intent of carrying tablets; speaking according to the matter, principle and fact unite—not as with poets, from whom one may cut a chapter to take meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign text links to carrying tablets; principle and fact align—not poetry, from which one may not cut a line at will.

sentences.zh: 古人求神之所非一，奉神之意無二，故廢桑主，重作栗主，既事理之，以明其一也。

translations.literal: The ancients sought the spirits in more than one place; the intent of honoring the spirits was one—hence the mulberry tablet was abandoned and the chestnut tablet remade; by reasoning the matter, this clarifies the one principle.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients sought spirits in more than one place with one intent—hence mulberry tablets were abandoned for chestnut remakes.

sentences.zh: 或又引《左氏傳》築郿凡例，謂「有宗廟先君之主曰都」，而立建主之論。

translations.literal: Some again cite the Zuo Commentary's general rule on building Fu, that "where there are ancestral tablets of the former lord it is called du," and set up the argument for establishing tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Some cite Zuo's Fu-building rule: "with former lords' tablets = du" to argue for new tablets.

sentences.zh: 按魯莊公二十八年冬，築郿，《左傳》為築發凡例，《谷梁》譏因藪澤之利，《公羊》稱避凶年造邑之嫌。

translations.literal: According to Lu, Duke Zhuang year 28 winter, building Fu—the Zuo Commentary made a general rule for building; Guliang criticized profiting from marsh and lake; Gongyang spoke of avoiding the suspicion of building a town in a famine year.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, Zhuang 28 winter: Zuo generalizes on building; Guliang criticized marsh profit; Gongyang cited famine-year suspicion.

sentences.zh: 三傳異同，左氏為短。

translations.literal: The three commentaries differ; the Zuo is inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The three commentaries differ; Zuo is weakest.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 當春秋二百年間，魯凡城二十四邑，唯郿一邑稱築，其二十三邑，豈皆有宗廟先君之主乎；

translations.literal: In the two hundred years of Spring and Autumn, Lu walled twenty-four settlements in all; only Fu was called "built"—did the other twenty-three all have ancestral tablets of former lords?
translations.idiomatic: In 240 years Lu walled twenty-four places; only Fu is "built"—did the other twenty-three all have ancestral tablets?

sentences.zh: 執此為建主之端，又非通論。

translations.literal: To take this as the opening for establishing tablets is again not sound general doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: That cannot ground a general doctrine of establishing tablets.

sentences.zh: 或又曰：「廢主之瘞，何以在於太微宮所藏之所；

translations.literal: Some also say: "Why bury abolished tablets in the Taiwei Palace storage place;
translations.idiomatic: Some ask why bury abolished tablets in Taiwei storage;

sentences.zh: 宜舍故依新，前已列矣。

translations.literal: one should abandon the old and follow the new—as already listed above."
translations.idiomatic: abandon old for new—as already argued."

sentences.zh: 」按瘞主之位有三：或於北牖之下，或在西階之間，廟之事也。

translations.literal: " According to the places for burying tablets there are three: under the north window, or between the western steps—matters of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Burying places: under the north window or between western steps—temple matters.

sentences.zh: 其不當立之主，但隨其所以瘞之。

translations.literal: Tablets that ought not to be established are buried only according to how they are to be buried.
translations.idiomatic: Improper tablets are buried as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 夫主瘞乎當立之廟，斯不然矣。

translations.literal: To bury tablets in a temple that should be established—this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Burying in a temple that should stand is wrong.

sentences.zh: 以在所而言，則太微宮所藏之所，與漢之寢園無異。

translations.literal: Speaking of the place, the Taiwei Palace storage is no different from Han's park-tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwei storage equals Han park-tombs.

sentences.zh: 歷代以降，建一都者多，兩都者少。

translations.literal: From successive ages downward, those who built one capital are many; two capitals are few.
translations.idiomatic: Most dynasties had one capital; two were rare.

sentences.zh: 今國家崇東西之宅，極嚴奉之典，而以各廟為疑，合以建都故事，以相質正，即周、漢是也。

translations.literal: Now the state honors both eastern and western residences to the utmost in solemn maintenance—yet doubts each temple; one should use the stories of capital-establishment to verify—Zhou and Han are the cases.
translations.idiomatic: The state honors both residences with full ritual—yet doubts each temple; Zhou and Han capital stories verify the case.

sentences.zh: 今詳議所征，究其年代，率皆一都之時，豈可以擬議，亦孰敢獻酬於其間？

translations.literal: Examining what the present deliberation cites, tracing their dates, they are almost all from times of one capital—how can they be applied to debate? Who would dare toast back and forth among them?
translations.idiomatic: Present citations are almost all one-capital eras—unfit for this debate; who would toast to them?

sentences.zh: 詳考經旨，古人謀寢必及於廟，未有設寢而不立廟者。

translations.literal: Examining the classics' intent in detail: the ancients in planning the sleeping palace always reached to the temple—never was there setting a palace without establishing a temple.
translations.idiomatic: Classics show: planning a palace always included the temple—never a palace without a temple.

sentences.zh: 國家承隋氏之弊，草創未暇，後雖建於垂拱，而事有所合。

translations.literal: The state inherited Sui's ruin; amid founding there was no leisure; though later built in the Chuigong era, the matter had its fitness.
translations.idiomatic: The state inherited Sui's ruin; founding left no leisure; Chuigong building fit the moment.

sentences.zh: 其後當干戈寧戢之歲，文物大備之朝，曆於十一聖，不議廢之。

translations.literal: Afterward, in the year when weapons were stilled and culture was fully equipped, through eleven sage rulers it was not debated for abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when arms rested and culture flourished, eleven sage reigns did not debate abolition.

sentences.zh: 豈不以事雖出於一時，廟有合立之理，而不可一一革也。

translations.literal: Was it not because though the matter arose in one moment, the temple had reason to be established and could not be abolished one by one?
translations.idiomatic: Though the matter was timely, the temple had reason to stand and could not be abolished piecemeal.

sentences.zh: 今洛都之制，上自宮殿樓觀，下及百辟之司，與西京無異。

translations.literal: Now Luoyang's institutions—from palaces and towers down to the hundred offices—differ in nothing from the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's institutions—from palaces down to the hundred offices—match the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 鑾輿之至也，雖廝役之賤，必歸其所理也。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrives, even the lowliest servants must return to their posts of duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrives, even servants return to their posts.

sentences.zh: 豈先帝之主，獨無其所安乎？

translations.literal: How can the former emperors' tablets alone have no place of rest?
translations.idiomatic: Can former emperors' tablets alone lack a resting place?

sentences.zh: 時也，虞主尚瘞，廢主宜然。

translations.literal: As to timing: the yu tablet is still buried; abolished tablets should be likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Timing: yu tablets are buried; abolished tablets should be too.

sentences.zh: 或以馬融、李舟二人稱「寢無傷於偕立，廟不妨於暫虛」，是則馬融、李舟，可法于宣尼矣。

translations.literal: Some cite Ma Rong and Li Zhou saying "the sleeping palace is not harmed by joint establishment; the temple is not hindered by temporary emptiness"—then Ma Rong and Li Zhou could be taken as models of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Some cite Ma Rong and Li Zhou: joint palace-building does no harm; temporary temple emptiness is allowed—making them Confucius's equals.

sentences.zh: 以此擬議，乖當則深。

translations.literal: To use this in deliberation—the deviation is deep.
translations.idiomatic: Applied to this debate, the error is deep.

sentences.zh: 或稱「凡邑有宗廟先君之主曰都，無曰邑，邑曰築，都曰城」者。

translations.literal: Some cite "Where a settlement has ancestral tablets of the former lord it is called du; without them it is called yi; yi is built, du is walled."
translations.idiomatic: Some cite: "With former lords' tablets = du; without = yi; yi is built, du is walled."

sentences.zh: 謹按春秋二百四十年間，惟郿一邑稱築。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that in the 240 years of Spring and Autumn only Fu was called "built."
translations.idiomatic: In 240 years of Spring and Autumn only Fu is "built."

sentences.zh: 如城郎、費之類，各有所因，或以他防，或以自固，謂之盡有宗廟，理則極非。

translations.literal: Cases like walling Lang and Fei each had their reasons—defense elsewhere or self-fortification—to say all had ancestral temples is utterly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Lang, Fei, and similar cases had other reasons—defense or fortification—not universal ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 或稱「聖主有復古之功，簡冊有考文之美，五帝不同樂，三王不同禮，遭時為法，因事制宜」。

translations.literal: Some cite "The sage ruler has the merit of restoring antiquity; the documents have the beauty of textual verification—five emperors had different music, three kings different ritual; encountering the times one makes law, according to affairs one sets measures."
translations.idiomatic: Some cite sage rulers restoring antiquity and documents verifying texts—five emperors, different music; three kings, different ritual; law for the times.

sentences.zh: 此則必作有為，非有司之事也。

translations.literal: This is work that must be undertaken—it is not the business of the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: That is positive statecraft—not routine office business.

sentences.zh: 如有司之職，但合一一據經；

translations.literal: If it is the duty of the offices, they should only unite in following the classics one by one;
translations.idiomatic: Offices should unite on the classics alone;

sentences.zh: 變禮從時，則須俟明詔也。

translations.literal: to change ritual according to the times requires awaiting a clear edict.
translations.idiomatic: changing ritual for the times awaits an explicit edict.

sentences.zh: 凡不修之證，略有七條：廟立因遷，一也；

translations.literal: The proofs against repair number seven in brief: temples established on removal—first;
translations.idiomatic: Seven proofs against repair: temples on removal—first;

sentences.zh: 已廢不舉，二也；

translations.literal: what has been abolished must not be raised—second;
translations.idiomatic: abolished rites must not be revived—second;

sentences.zh: 廟不可虛，三也；

translations.literal: temples cannot be empty—third;
translations.idiomatic: empty temples forbidden—third;

sentences.zh: 非時不造主，四也；

translations.literal: tablets are not made out of season—fourth;
translations.idiomatic: no out-of-season tablet-making—fourth;

sentences.zh: 合載遷主行，五也；

translations.literal: carrying the removed-chamber tablet on tour—fifth;
translations.idiomatic: Carrying the removed-chamber tablet on tour—fifth;

sentences.zh: 尊無二上，六也；

translations.literal: no second supreme in honor—sixth;
translations.idiomatic: No second supreme in honor—sixth;

sentences.zh: 《六典》不書，七也。

translations.literal: not recorded in the Six Institutions—seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Not recorded in the Six Institutions—seventh.

sentences.zh: 謹按文王遷豐立廟，武王遷鎬立廟，成王遷洛立廟，今東都不因遷而欲立廟，是違因遷立廟也。

translations.literal: I respectfully note King Wen moved to Feng and established a temple, King Wu to Hao, King Cheng to Luo—now the Eastern Capital would build a temple without removal, violating temples on removal.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen, Wu, and Cheng each established temples on removal; the Eastern Capital would build without removal—violating that rule.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮記》曰：「凡祭，有其廢之，莫敢舉也。

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the Record of Rites: "In all sacrifice, what has been abolished—none dares raise it.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites: "What has been abolished in sacrifice—none dares raise; what has been raised—none dares abolish."

sentences.zh: 有其舉之，莫敢廢也。

translations.literal: What has been raised—none dares abolish."
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital Grand Temple has been abandoned eight reigns; rebuilding violates "abolished must not be raised."

sentences.zh: 」今東都太廟，廢已八朝，若果立之，是違已廢不舉也。

translations.literal: " Now the Eastern Capital Grand Temple has been abolished through eight reigns; if truly rebuilt, this violates "abolished must not be raised."
translations.idiomatic: The Record: "Seven and five temples must have no empty tablet."

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮記》曰：「當七廟五廟無虛主。

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the Record of Rites: "The seven temples and five temples must have no empty tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Empty temples violate "temples cannot be empty."

sentences.zh: 」今欲立虛廟，是違廟不可虛也。

translations.literal: " To wish empty temples violates "temples cannot be empty."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary: "On dingchou Duke Xi's tablet was made—untimely."

sentences.zh: 謹按《左傳》：「丁丑，作僖公主。

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the Zuo Commentary: "On dingchou, Duke Xi's tablet was made.
translations.idiomatic: The Record: "Late sacrifice is still ritual."

sentences.zh: 書不時也。

translations.literal: The record is untimely."
translations.idiomatic: Even timely rites are abandoned when late—may improper tablets be made?

sentences.zh: 」《記》又曰：「過時不祭，禮也。

translations.literal: The Record also says: "Sacrifice out of season is ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Out-of-season tablet-making violates the rule.

sentences.zh: 」合禮之祭，過時猶廢，非禮之主，可以作乎？

translations.literal: " Even proper sacrifice is abandoned when late—may an improper tablet be made?
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi Questions: "Did armies carry the removed-chamber tablet?"

sentences.zh: 今欲非時作主，是違非時不作主也。

translations.literal: Now to make tablets out of season violates "no out-of-season tablet-making."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius: On tour the removed-chamber tablet rides on the fasting carriage—honor must be present.

sentences.zh: 謹按《曾子問》：「古者師行以遷廟主行乎？

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the Zengzi Questions: "In antiquity did armies on campaign carry the removed-chamber tablet?"
translations.idiomatic: Taking all seven temples' tablets is wrong.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：天子巡狩，必以遷廟主行，載于齋車，言必有尊也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: On imperial tour the removed-chamber tablet must be carried, loaded on the fasting carriage—meaning there must be what is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Huang: "Removed-chamber tablet = one newly removed chamber only."

sentences.zh: 今也取七廟之主以行，則失之矣。

translations.literal: Now to take all seven temples' tablets on tour is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying all temples' tablets violates that rule.
