translations.idiomatic: Two yin sacrifices in five years match Heaven's pattern—one great, one small. Learned opinion holds that the lesser excludes ministers, the greater includes meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 今禮禘無功臣，誠謂禮不可易。

translations.literal: Now the rite has di without meritorious ministers; your subject truly holds the rite cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: The present rite omits meritorious ministers from di; the rite should not be changed.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔改令從禮。

translations.literal: " An edict then ordered the regulations changed to follow the rite.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the rules brought into line with ritual.

sentences.zh: 至開元中改修禮，復令禘祫俱以功臣配饗焉。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, when the rites were revised, di and xia were again both made to include meritorious ministers in accompanying offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaiyuan revised the rites, di and xia again both assigned meritorious ministers accompanying offerings.

sentences.zh: 高宗上元三年十月，將祫享於太廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Shangyuan under Emperor Gaozong, a xia offering was to be performed at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong, Shangyuan 3, tenth month: a Grand Temple xia was planned.

sentences.zh: 時議者以《禮緯》「三年一祫，五年一禘」《公羊傳》雲「五年而再殷祭」，議交互莫能斷決。

translations.literal: Deliberators cited the Rites Apocrypha, "xia once in three years, di once in five years," and the Gongyang Commentary, "two yin sacrifices in five years"; the arguments crossed and none could decide.
translations.idiomatic: Debates cited the Rites Apocrypha ("xia every three years, di every five") and Gongyang ("two yin sacrifices in five years") and could not be resolved.

sentences.zh: 太學博士史璨等議曰：「按《禮記正義》引鄭玄《禘祫志》云：'《春秋》：僖公三十三年十二月薨。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Shi Can and others deliberated: "According to the Correct Meaning of the Book of Rites citing Zheng Xuan's Record of Di and Xia: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals: Duke Xi died in the twelfth month of his thirty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Shi Can et al. argued: per the Book of Rites citing Zheng Xuan's Di-Xia Record, Spring and Autumn records Duke Xi's death in month 12, year 33.

sentences.zh: 文公二年八月丁卯，大享於太廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duke Wen, eighth month, dingmao, a great offering was made at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen year 2, month 8, dingmao: a great offering at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》云：大享者何？

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: What is a great offering?
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang asks: what is a great offering?

sentences.zh: 祫也。

translations.literal: It is xia.
translations.idiomatic: Xia.

sentences.zh: '是三年喪畢，新君二年當祫，明年當禘於群廟。

translations.literal: ' When the three-year mourning was complete, in the new ruler's second year there should be xia; the next year di at the group temples.
translations.idiomatic: After three-year mourning, year 2 is xia; year 3 is di at the group temples.

sentences.zh: 僖公、宣公八年皆有禘，則後禘去前禘五年。

translations.literal: Dukes Xi and Xuan both had di in their eighth years; thus the later di was five years from the earlier di.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Xuan each held di in year 8—five years between successive di.

sentences.zh: 以此定之，則新君二年祫，三年禘。

translations.literal: By this determination, a new ruler has xia in year 2 and di in year 3.
translations.idiomatic: Thus a new ruler: xia year 2, di year 3.

sentences.zh: 自爾已後，五年而再殷祭，則六年當祫，八年當禘。

translations.literal: Thereafter, with two yin sacrifices in five years, year 6 should be xia and year 8 di.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, two yin sacrifices in five years means xia in year 6 and di in year 8.

sentences.zh: 又昭公十年，齊歸薨，至十三年喪畢當祫，為平丘之會，冬，公如晉。

translations.literal: Again, in Duke Zhao's tenth year Qi Gui died; by the thirteenth year mourning was complete and xia was due, but because of the Pingqiu conference, in winter the duke went to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao year 10: Qi Gui died; mourning ended year 13 when xia was due, but the Pingqiu meeting sent the duke to Jin that winter.

sentences.zh: 至十四年祫，十五年禘《傳》雲'有事于武宮'是也。

translations.literal: Xia came in year 14 and di in year 15—the Commentary's "there were affairs at the Martial Shrine" refers to this.
translations.idiomatic: Xia in year 14, di in year 15—the "affairs at the Martial Shrine" passage applies.

sentences.zh: 至十八年祫，二十年禘。

translations.literal: Xia in year 18, di in year 20.
translations.idiomatic: Xia year 18, di year 20.

sentences.zh: 二十三年祫，二十五年禘。

translations.literal: Xia in year 23, di in year 25.
translations.idiomatic: Xia year 23, di year 25.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十五年'有事于襄宮'是也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao year 25, "there were affairs at the Xiang Shrine," refers to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao year 25, "affairs at the Xiang Shrine," is the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 如上所雲，則禘已後隔三年祫，已後隔二年禘。

translations.literal: As stated above, after di, xia follows three years later; after xia, di follows two years later.
translations.idiomatic: After di, xia is three years later; after xia, di is two years later.

sentences.zh: 此則有合禮經，不違《傳》義。

translations.literal: This accords with the ritual classics and does not violate the Commentary's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: This fits the classics and Gongyang's sense.

sentences.zh: 」自此依璨等議為定。

translations.literal: " From this, Can and others' deliberation was adopted as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: " Can's view became the fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 開元六年秋，睿宗喪畢，祫享於太廟。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth Kaiyuan year, when Emperor Ruizong's mourning was complete, xia was performed at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 6 autumn: after Ruizong's mourning, Grand Temple xia was held.

sentences.zh: 自後又相承三年一祫，五年一禘，各自計年，不相通數。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was again handed down as xia once in three years and di once in five years, each counted separately, not reckoned together.
translations.idiomatic: Later practice counted xia every three years and di every five, separately—not jointly.

sentences.zh: 至二十七年，凡經五禘、七祫。

translations.literal: By year 27, there had been five di and seven xia in all.
translations.idiomatic: By year 27 there had been five di and seven xia.

sentences.zh: 其年夏禘訖，冬又當祫。

translations.literal: That year, after summer di was complete, winter again called for xia.
translations.idiomatic: That year summer di had just ended when winter again required xia.

sentences.zh: 太常議曰：

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported:

sentences.zh: 禘祫二禮，俱為殷祭，祫為合食祖廟，禘謂諦序尊卑。

translations.literal: The two rites di and xia are both yin sacrifices: xia is combined feasting at the ancestral temple; di means ordering ranks of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia are both yin sacrifices: xia combines ancestors at the Grand Temple; di orders seniority.

sentences.zh: 申先君逮下之慈，成群嗣奉親之孝，事異常享，有時行之。

translations.literal: They extend the former ruler's kindness reaching down and gather the filial piety of descendants in serving kin—unlike regular offerings, they are performed at set times.
translations.idiomatic: They extend a late ruler's care and gather heirs' filial service—unlike seasonal rites, performed only at appointed times.

sentences.zh: 然而祭不欲數，數則黷；

translations.literal: Yet offerings should not be frequent; frequency breeds irreverence;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice should not be too frequent, lest it become irreverent;

sentences.zh: 亦不欲疏，疏則怠。

translations.literal: nor should they be too sparse, lest neglect arise.
translations.idiomatic: nor too sparse, lest it breed neglect.

sentences.zh: 故王者法諸天道，制祀典焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the king models Heaven's Way and fixes the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Kings therefore model Heaven and fix the sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 烝嘗象時，禘祫如閏。

translations.literal: Zheng and chang mirror the seasons; di and xia are like intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and chang follow the seasons; di and xia follow the intercalary pattern.

sentences.zh: 五歲再閏，天道大成，宗廟法之，再為殷祭者也。

translations.literal: Two intercalations in five years complete Heaven's great pattern; the ancestral temple follows this with two yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Two intercalations in five years complete Heaven's cycle; the temple mirrors this with two yin sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮記·王制》、《周官·宗伯》，鄭玄注解，高堂所議，並雲「國君嗣位，三年喪畢，祫于太祖。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the "Royal Regulations" in the Book of Rites, the Director of Ritual in the Offices of Zhou, Zheng Xuan's commentary, and Gaotang's deliberation—all say: "When a state lord succeeds, after three-year mourning is complete, xia at the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Per Book of Rites "Royal Regulations," Zhou Offices Director of Ritual, Zheng Xuan, and Gaotang: after succession and three-year mourning, xia at the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 明年禘於群廟。

translations.literal: The next year di at the group temples.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, di at the group temples.

sentences.zh: 自爾已後，五年再殷，一祫一禘。

translations.literal: Thereafter, two yin sacrifices in five years—one xia and one di."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter two yin sacrifices in five years—one xia, one di."

sentences.zh: 」漢、魏故事，貞觀實錄，並用此禮。

translations.literal: Han and Wei precedents and the Veritable Records of Zhenguan all used this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, and Zhenguan records all followed this schedule.

sentences.zh: 又按《禮緯》及《魯禮禘祫注》雲，三年一祫，五年一禘，所謂五年而再殷祭也。

translations.literal: Again according to the Rites Apocrypha and the Lu Rites Commentary on Di and Xia: xia once in three years, di once in five years—what is called two yin sacrifices in five years.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Apocrypha and Lu commentary likewise say xia every three years and di every five—the "two yin sacrifices in five years."

sentences.zh: 又按《白虎通》及《五經通義》、許慎《異義》、何休《春秋》、賀循《祭議》，並雲三年一禘。

translations.literal: Again according to the Baihu Treatise, Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics, Xu Shen's Dissenting Views, He Xiu's Spring and Autumn, and He Xun's Sacrificial Deliberation—all say di once in three years.
translations.idiomatic: Baihu, Five Classics Meaning, Xu Shen, He Xiu, and He Xun's Sacrificial Deliberation all say di every three years.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why (idiomatic).

sentences.zh: 以為三年一閏，天道小備，五年再閏，天道大備故也。

translations.literal: They hold that one intercalation in three years means Heaven's small completion; two intercalations in five years means Heaven's great completion.
translations.idiomatic: One intercalation in three years is Heaven's lesser cycle; two in five is the greater—hence the count.

sentences.zh: 此則五年再殷，通計其數，一祫一禘，迭相乘矣。

translations.literal: Thus two yin sacrifices in five years, reckoned through the whole number, one xia and one di alternate in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Two yin sacrifices in five years mean one xia and one di alternating through the whole period.

sentences.zh: 今太廟禘祫，各自數年，兩岐俱下，不相通計。

translations.literal: Now Grand Temple di and xia each count their own years; two branches are issued, not reckoned together.
translations.idiomatic: Today di and xia are counted separately—two schedules, not one integrated cycle.

sentences.zh: 或比年頻合，或同歲再序，或一禘之後，並為再祫，或五年之內，驟有三殷。

translations.literal: Sometimes offerings cluster in successive years, or twice in one year; sometimes after one di there are two xia, or within five years suddenly three yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings sometimes pile up year after year or twice in one year; one di may be followed by two xia, or three yin sacrifices within five years.

sentences.zh: 法天象閏之期，既違其度；

translations.literal: The period modeled on Heaven's intercalary pattern is already violated;
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary pattern is already broken;

sentences.zh: 五歲再殷之制，數又不同。

translations.literal: the rule of two yin sacrifices in five years also differs in number.
translations.idiomatic: and the "two yin sacrifices in five years" count no longer holds.

sentences.zh: 求之禮文，頗為乖失。

translations.literal: Sought in ritual texts, it is quite at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against ritual text, the practice is seriously awry.

sentences.zh: 說者或云：「禘祫二禮，大小不侔，祭名有殊，年數相舛。

translations.literal: Some explainers say: "The two rites di and xia differ in greatness; the sacrifice names differ and the year-counts cross.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue di and xia differ in rank and name, so their year-counts cannot be unified.

sentences.zh: 祫以三紀，抵小而合；

translations.literal: Xia uses three cycles, reaching the small and combining;
translations.idiomatic: Xia uses three cycles to reach the lesser union;

sentences.zh: 禘以五斷，至十而周。

translations.literal: di uses five divisions, reaching ten to complete the cycle.
translations.idiomatic: di uses five divisions to complete a ten-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 有茲參差，難以通計。

translations.literal: With such discrepancy, it is hard to reckon together."
translations.idiomatic: Such discrepancy, they say, forbids a single reckoning."

sentences.zh: 」竊以三祫五禘之說，本出《禮緯》，五歲再殷之數，同在其篇，會通二文，非相詭也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the theory of three xia and five di comes from the Rites Apocrypha; the count of two yin sacrifices in five years is in the same chapter—harmonizing the two texts, they do not contradict.
translations.idiomatic: The "three xia, five di" theory and "two yin sacrifices in five years" both come from the Rites Apocrypha and can be harmonized.

sentences.zh: 蓋以禘後置祫，二周有半，舉以全數，謂之三年，譬如三年一閏，只用三十二月也。

translations.literal: It is that after di, xia is placed two and a half cycles later; taking the full number, it is called three years—like one intercalation in three years using only thirty-six months.
translations.idiomatic: After di, xia follows two and a half cycles; rounded to a full number that is "three years," as one intercalation uses thirty-six months.

sentences.zh: 其禘祫異稱，各隨四時，秋冬為祫，春夏為禘。

translations.literal: Di and xia have different names, each following the four seasons: autumn-winter for xia, spring-summer for di.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia take different names by season—xia in autumn-winter, di in spring-summer.

sentences.zh: 祭名雖異，為殷則同，譬如礿、祠、烝、嘗，其體一也。

translations.literal: Though the sacrifice names differ, as yin sacrifices they are the same—like yue, ci, zheng, and chang, their substance is one.
translations.idiomatic: Names differ, but as yin sacrifices they are one—like yue, ci, zheng, and chang.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄謂祫大禘小，傳或謂祫小禘大，肆陳之間，或有增減，通計之義，初無異同。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan holds xia is great and di small; some commentaries hold xia small and di great—in the array of offerings there may be increase or decrease, but in reckoning together there is fundamentally no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says xia is greater, some texts say di is greater; offerings may vary, but the combined reckoning is the same.

sentences.zh: 蓋象閏之法，相傳久矣。

translations.literal: The method modeled on intercalation has been transmitted long.
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary model is ancient.

sentences.zh: 惟晉代陳舒有三年一殷之議，自五年、八年又十一、十四，尋其議文所引，亦以象閏為言。

translations.literal: Only Jin-era Chen Shu had a deliberation of one yin sacrifice in three years—from five, eight, eleven, and fourteen; tracing his deliberation's citations, he too spoke of modeling intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jin's Chen Shu argued one yin sacrifice every three years (years 5, 8, 11, 14), still citing the intercalary model.

sentences.zh: 且六歲再殷，何名象閏？

translations.literal: Yet two yin sacrifices in six years—how can it be called modeling intercalation?
translations.idiomatic: Two yin sacrifices in six years is not "modeling intercalation."

sentences.zh: 五年一禘，又奚所施？

translations.literal: And di once in five years—where is it applied?
translations.idiomatic: Nor does "di every five years" fit.

sentences.zh: 矛盾之說，固難憑也。

translations.literal: Contradictory theories are indeed hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Contradictory theories cannot be relied on.

sentences.zh: 夫以法天之度，既有指歸，稽古之理，若茲昭著。

translations.literal: Since the measure that models Heaven already has its direction, and investigating antiquity the principle is so clear.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's measure has a clear direction; antiquity confirms it.

sentences.zh: 禘祫二祭，通計明矣。

translations.literal: Reckoning di and xia together is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Joint reckoning of di and xia is plain.

sentences.zh: 今請以開元二十七年己卯四月禘，至辛巳年十月祫，至甲申年四月又禘，至丙戌年十月又祫，至己丑年四月又禘，至辛卯年十月又祫。

translations.literal: We now ask to take Kaiyuan 27, year jimao, fourth month for di; to year xinsi tenth month for xia; to year jiashen fourth month again di; to year bingxu tenth month again xia; to year jichou fourth month again di; to year xinmao tenth month again xia.
translations.idiomatic: Proposed schedule from Kaiyuan 27 jimao month 4 di, through xinsi month 10 xia, jiashen month 4 di, bingxu month 10 xia, jichou month 4 di, xinmao month 10 xia.

sentences.zh: 自此五年再殷，周而復始。

translations.literal: From this, two yin sacrifices in five years, cycling and beginning again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter two yin sacrifices in five years, cycling indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 又禘祫之說，非唯一家，五歲再殷之文，既相師矣，法天象閏之理，大抵亦同。

translations.literal: Again, theories of di and xia are not from one school alone; texts on two yin sacrifices in five years already follow one another, and the principle of modeling Heaven's intercalation is broadly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Di-xia theory has many schools, but "two yin sacrifices in five years" and the intercalary model largely agree.

sentences.zh: 而禘後置祫，或近或遠，盈縮之度，有二法焉：鄭玄宗高堂，則先三而後二；

translations.literal: Yet placing xia after di may be near or far; in the measure of expansion and contraction there are two methods: Zheng Xuan and Gaotang place three first then two;
translations.idiomatic: After di, xia may be nearer or farther. Zheng Xuan and Gaotang put "three" before "two";

sentences.zh: 徐邈之議，則先二而後三。

translations.literal: Xu Miao's deliberation puts two first then three.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao puts "two" before "three."

sentences.zh: 謹按鄭氏所注，先三之法，約三祫五禘之文，存三歲五年之位。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to Zheng's commentary, the method of three first approximates the text of three xia and five di, preserving the positions of three years and five years.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's "three first" method fits the three-xia five-di texts and preserves the three-year and five-year slots.

sentences.zh: 以為甲年既禘，丁年當祫，己年又禘，壬年又祫，甲年又禘，丁年又祫，周而復始，以此相承。

translations.literal: It holds that if in year jia there is di, in year ding there should be xia, in year ji again di, in year ren again xia, in year jia again di, in year ding again xia—cycling and beginning again, handed down thus.
translations.idiomatic: On Zheng's scheme: jia year di, ding xia, ji di, ren xia, and repeat—jia di, ding xia, and so on.

sentences.zh: 祫後去禘，十有八月而近，禘後去祫，三十二月而遙，分析不均，粗於算矣。

translations.literal: From xia to di is eighteen months—near; from di to xia thirty-six months—far; the analysis is uneven and crude in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Xia to di is 18 months (too near); di to xia is 36 (too far)—uneven spacing.

sentences.zh: 假如攻乎異端，置祫於秋，則三十九月為前，二十一月為後，雖小有愈，其間尚偏。

translations.literal: Suppose one pursues heterodox views and places xia in autumn: then thirty-nine months before and twenty-one after—though slightly better, the interval is still skewed.
translations.idiomatic: Placing xia in autumn yields 39 months before and 21 after—slightly better but still skewed.

sentences.zh: 竊據本文，皆云象閏，二閏相去，則平分矣。

translations.literal: Your subject relies on the original texts, which all say "model intercalation"; two intercalations apart are then evenly divided.
translations.idiomatic: The texts all say "model intercalation"; two intercalations apart divide evenly.

sentences.zh: 兩殷之序，何不等耶？

translations.literal: Why should the order of the two yin sacrifices be unequal?
translations.idiomatic: Why should the two yin sacrifices be unequal?

sentences.zh: 且又三年之言，本舉全數，二周有半，實准三年，於此置祫，不違文矣，何必拘滯隔三正乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, "three years" originally states the full number; two and a half cycles truly equals three years—placing xia here does not violate the text; why must one rigidly insist on skipping three first months?
translations.idiomatic: "Three years" is a round number for two and a half cycles; placing xia here does not violate the text—why insist on three whole years?

sentences.zh: 蓋千慮一失，通儒之蔽也。

translations.literal: It is the one flaw in a thousand deliberations—the blind spot of accomplished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Even great scholars err once in a thousand deliberations.

sentences.zh: 徐氏之議，有異於是，研核周審，最為可憑。

translations.literal: Xu's deliberation differs from this; examined thoroughly, it is most reliable.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao's view differs and, on close review, is most reliable.

sentences.zh: 以為二禘相去，為月六十，中分三十，置一祫焉。

translations.literal: It holds that two di are sixty months apart; halve to thirty and place one xia.
translations.idiomatic: Two di are 60 months apart; halve to 30 and insert one xia.

sentences.zh: 若甲年夏禘，丙年冬祫，有象閏法，毫釐不偏。

translations.literal: If in year jia summer di, in year bing winter xia, the intercalary model is followed without the slightest deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Jia summer di, bing winter xia—exact intercalary spacing.

sentences.zh: 三年一祫之文，既無乖越；

translations.literal: The text "xia once in three years" is not violated;
translations.idiomatic: This satisfies "xia every three years";

sentences.zh: 五歲再殷之制，疏數有均。

translations.literal: the rule of two yin sacrifices in five years has even spacing in its count.
translations.idiomatic: and keeps "two yin sacrifices in five years" evenly spaced.

sentences.zh: 校之諸儒，義實長久。

translations.literal: Compared with the various Ru, the meaning is truly enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Among Ru traditions it is the soundest long-term reading.

sentences.zh: 今請依據以定二殷，預推祭月，周而復始。

translations.literal: We now ask to fix the two yin sacrifices on this basis, projecting sacrifice months in advance, cycling and beginning again.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to fix the two yin sacrifices on this basis, project the months, and cycle indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎崔宗之駁下太常，令更詳議，令集賢學士陸善經等更加詳核，善經亦以其議為允。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Cui Zongzhi rebutted and sent the matter down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for further deliberation; Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies Lu Shanqing and others were ordered to examine further, and Shanqing also approved this deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zongzhi of the Ministry of Rites objected and sent the case back to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Lu Shanqing and other academicians reviewed it and approved.

sentences.zh: 於是太常卿韋縚奏曰：「禮有禘祫，俱稱殷祭，二法更用，鱗次相承。

translations.literal: Thereupon Director Wei Zong memorialized: "The rites provide di and xia, both called yin sacrifices; the two methods alternate in scale-like succession.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wei Zong reported: di and xia are both yin sacrifices, alternating in regular succession.

sentences.zh: 或云五歲再殷，一禘一祫。

translations.literal: Some say two yin sacrifices in five years—one di and one xia.
translations.idiomatic: Some say two yin sacrifices in five years—one di, one xia.

sentences.zh: 或云三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: Some say xia once in three years, di once in five years.
translations.idiomatic: Others say xia every three years and di every five.

sentences.zh: 法天象閏，大趣皆同。

translations.literal: Modeling Heaven's intercalation—the main tendency is the same.
translations.idiomatic: All model Heaven's intercalation in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 皆以太廟禘祫，計年有差，考于經傳，微有所乖。

translations.literal: All because Grand Temple di and xia count years differently; examined against classics and commentaries, there is slight deviation.
translations.idiomatic: But because the Grand Temple counts di and xia separately, the practice slightly departs from the classics.

sentences.zh: 頃在四月，已行禘享，今指孟冬，又申祫儀，合食禮頻，恐違先典。

translations.literal: Recently in the fourth month, di was already performed; now pointing to mid-winter, xia rites are again proposed—combined feasting too frequent, fearing violation of former canons.
translations.idiomatic: Di was just performed in the fourth month; mid-winter xia is now proposed—combined feasting too often, against ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下能事畢舉，舊物咸甄，宗祏祗慎之時，經訓申明之日。

translations.literal: Your subject notes that Your Majesty's accomplishments are complete and old things all restored—at a time when the ancestral temple is reverently cautious and canonical teaching is clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has restored the rites; this is the moment to clarify ancestral practice.

sentences.zh: 臣等忝在持禮，職司討論，輒據舊文，定其倫序。

translations.literal: We who disgracefully hold ritual office are charged with deliberation and venture according to old texts to fix the sequence.
translations.idiomatic: We in ritual office venture to fix the sequence from old texts.

sentences.zh: 請以今年夏禘，便為殷祭之源，自此之後，禘、祫相代，五年再殷，周而復始。

translations.literal: We ask that this year's summer di serve as the source of yin sacrifices; from this onward di and xia alternate, two yin sacrifices in five years, cycling and beginning again.
translations.idiomatic: Let this summer's di begin the cycle; thereafter di and xia alternate every five years.

sentences.zh: 其今年冬祫，准禮合停，望令所司但行時享，即嚴禋不黷，庶合舊儀。

translations.literal: This year's winter xia should by the rite be stopped; we hope the responsible offices will perform only the seasonal offering, so solemn sacrifice is not irreverent and the old rite is approximated.
translations.idiomatic: This winter's xia should be omitted; only seasonal offerings should be held, avoiding irreverent frequency.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，天寶八年閏六月六日敕文：「禘祫之禮，以存序位，質文之變，蓋取隨時。

translations.literal: Former practice: edict of Tianbao 8, intercalary sixth month, sixth day: "The rites of di and xia preserve ordered rank; changes in substance and ornament take their cue from the times.
translations.idiomatic: Former practice—Tianbao 8, intercalary month 6, day 6 edict: "Di and xia preserve rank; ornament may change with the times.

sentences.zh: 國家系本仙宗，業承聖祖，重熙累盛，既錫無疆之休，合享登神，思弘不易之典。

translations.literal: The state traces its origin to the Immortal Ancestor and inherits the sage forebear; repeated glory and accumulated splendor have already been granted boundless blessing; combined offerings ascend to the spirits—we think to expand the unchanging canon.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty descends from the Immortal Ancestor and inherits sage forebears; we seek to uphold the unchanging canon of ascent and offering.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，每禘祫並于太清宮聖祖前設位序正，上以明陟配之禮，欽若玄象，下以盡虔祭之誠，無違至道。

translations.literal: From now on, at every di and xia, set ranks in order before the Sage Ancestor at the Temple of Supreme Clarity, above to clarify the rite of ascent and matching, reverently conforming to the dark heavens, below to fulfill the sincerity of reverent sacrifice, not departing from the ultimate Way.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at each di and xia arrange ranks before the Sage Ancestor at Supreme Clarity, clarifying ascent and matching above and full sincerity below.

sentences.zh: 比來每緣禘祫，時享則停，事雖適於從宜，禮或虧於必備。

translations.literal: Recently, whenever di and xia occurred, seasonal offerings were suspended; though the affair suited expedience, the rite perhaps fell short of what must be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Lately seasonal offerings stopped during di and xia—expedient but incomplete.

sentences.zh: 已後每緣禘祫，其常享以素饌，三焚香以代三獻。」

translations.literal: Hereafter whenever di and xia occur, regular offerings shall use plain food; three burnings of incense replace the three presentations."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter during di and xia, regular offerings use plain food and three incense burnings replace three presentations."

sentences.zh: 建中二年九月四日，太常博士陳京上疏言：「今年十月，祫享太廟，併合饗遷廟獻祖、懿祖二神主。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the ninth month of the second Jianzhong year, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chen Jing memorialized: "This tenth month, xia at the Grand Temple should jointly feast the relocated temple spirit tablets of the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong 2, month 9, day 4: Erudite Chen Jing urged that the tenth-month Grand Temple xia include the Offerings and Eminence ancestors' relocated tablets.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，毀廟之主，陳于太祖，未毀廟之主，皆升合食于太祖。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals: tablets of destroyed temples are displayed before the Grand Ancestor; tablets of temples not yet destroyed all ascend for combined feasting at the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn: destroyed temples' tablets are set before the Grand Ancestor; others ascend for combined feasting.

sentences.zh: 太祖之位，在西而東向，其下子孫，昭穆相對，南北為別，初無毀廟遷主不享之文。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's position faces east from the west; descendants below are arranged zhao and mu opposite, south and north as distinction—originally there is no text of destroyed temples' relocated tablets not receiving offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor faces east; descendants are arranged in zhao-mu rows—no rule excludes relocated tablets of destroyed shrines.

sentences.zh: 征是禮也，自于周室，而國朝祀典，當與周異。

translations.literal: Examining this rite, from the Zhou house onward, yet our dynasty's sacrificial canon ought to differ from Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou did thus, but Tang ritual should differ.

sentences.zh: 且周以後稷配天，為始封之祖，而下乃立廟。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhou took Hou Ji to match Heaven as the ancestor of the first enfeoffment, and only below him established temples.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou matched Hou Ji to Heaven as first enfeoffment ancestor, then built lower temples.

sentences.zh: 廟毀主遷，皆在太祖之後。

translations.literal: When temples were destroyed and tablets moved, all were after the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Destroyed shrines and moved tablets all stood after the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 禘祫之時，無先于太廟太祖者。

translations.literal: At di and xia, none preceded the Grand Ancestor in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At di and xia nothing preceded the Grand Temple Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 正太祖東向之位，全其尊而不疑。

translations.literal: Correcting the Grand Ancestor's east-facing position preserves his honor without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor's east-facing seat preserves unquestioned honor.

sentences.zh: 然今年十月祫饗太廟，伏請據魏、晉舊制為比，則構築別廟。

translations.literal: Yet this tenth month's Grand Temple xia feast—your subject asks to take Wei and Jin old institutions as comparison and build separate temples.
translations.idiomatic: For this tenth-month xia, Chen asks to follow Wei-Jin precedent and build separate temples.

sentences.zh: 東晉以征西等四府君為別廟，至禘祫之時，則于太廟正太祖之位以申其尊，別廟祭高皇、太皇、征西等四府君以敘其親。

translations.literal: Eastern Jin took the four lords such as the Western Campaign General as separate temples; at di and xia they corrected the Grand Ancestor's position in the Grand Temple to assert his honor, while the separate temples sacrificed to the High Emperor, Grand Emperor, Western Campaign General, and the other four lords to express kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin gave four forebears separate temples; at di and xia the Grand Ancestor kept honor in the Grand Temple while separate temples served the remote forebears.

sentences.zh: 伏以國家若用此義，則宜別為獻祖、懿祖立廟，禘祫祭之，以重其親；

translations.literal: Your subject holds that if the state uses this principle, separate temples should be built for the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence and they should receive di and xia;
translations.idiomatic: Tang should build separate temples for Offerings and Eminence and sacrifice to them at di and xia;

sentences.zh: 則太祖于太廟遂居東向，以全其尊。

translations.literal: then the Grand Ancestor in the Grand Temple would occupy the east-facing position to preserve his full honor.
translations.idiomatic: so the Grand Ancestor can face east in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 伏以德明、興聖二皇帝，曩立廟，至禘祫之時，常用饗禮，今則別廟之制，使就興聖廟藏祔為宜。

translations.literal: Your subject notes the two emperors Deming and Xingsheng formerly had temples; at di and xia regular feast rites were commonly used—now the separate-temple system should have enshrinement in the Xingsheng temple as fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Deming and Xingsheng once had their own temples; separate shrines should enshrine the tablets in the Xingsheng temple."

sentences.zh: 」敕下尚書省百僚集議。

translations.literal: " An edict sent the matter down to the Department of State Affairs for assembly deliberation by the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene deliberation.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使太子少師顏真卿議曰：「議者或云獻祖、懿祖親遠廟遷，不當祫享，宜永閟西夾室。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Ritual Protocol, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent Yan Zhenqing, deliberated: "Some deliberators say the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence, kin distant and temples moved, should not receive xia and ought permanently to be shut in the western side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing argued: some said Offerings and Eminence, being remote, should not join xia and should stay shut in the western side chambers;

sentences.zh: 又議者雲二祖宜同祫享，于太祖並昭穆，而空太祖東向之位。

translations.literal: Others say the two ancestors should share xia, ranking zhao and mu with the Grand Ancestor while leaving the Grand Ancestor's east-facing position empty.
translations.idiomatic: others that both should share xia with the Grand Ancestor in zhao-mu order while leaving his east seat empty;

sentences.zh: 又議者雲，二祖若同袷享，即太祖之位永不得正，宜奉遷二祖神主祔藏于德明皇帝廟。

translations.literal: Others say if the two ancestors share xia, the Grand Ancestor's position can never be corrected; the two ancestors' tablets should be moved and enshrined in the temple of Emperor Deming."
translations.idiomatic: others that if they share xia the Grand Ancestor can never face east and both tablets should move to the Deming temple."

sentences.zh: 臣伏以三議俱未為允。

translations.literal: Your subject holds all three deliberations are not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held all three views unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 且禮經殘缺，既無明據，儒者能方義類，斟酌其中，則可舉而行之，蓋協於正也。

translations.literal: The ritual classics are damaged and lack clear authority; if scholars can compare categories and weigh among them, then it may be enacted—this broadly accords with rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: The classics are incomplete; where scholars analogize and weigh categories, practice may proceed in accord with right principle.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太祖景皇帝以受命始封之功，處百代不遷之廟，配天崇享，是極尊嚴。

translations.literal: Your subject notes Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing, by merit of receiving the mandate at first enfeoffment, occupies the temple of a hundred generations without removal, matching Heaven in lofty offering—this is ultimate honor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing, first enfeoffment and mandate, occupies the immovable shrine and matches Heaven—ultimate honor.

sentences.zh: 且至禘祫之時，暫居昭穆之位，屈己申孝，敬奉祖宗，緣齒族之禮，廣尊先之道，此實太祖明神烝烝之本意，亦所以化被天下，率循孝悌也。

translations.literal: At di and xia he temporarily takes the zhao-mu position, lowering himself to express filial piety and reverently serving the ancestors—by the rite of kin order, broadening the way of honoring forebears; this is truly the Grand Ancestor's bright intent of teeming blessing, and also how to transform the realm and lead all to filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At di and xia he temporarily takes a zhao-mu place, humbling himself to honor ancestors—his teeming intent and the empire's model of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 請依晉蔡謨等議，至十月祫享之日奉獻祖神主居東向之位，自懿祖、太祖洎諸祖宗，遵左昭右穆之列。

translations.literal: We ask to follow Jin Cai Mo and others' deliberation: on the day of the tenth-month xia offering, place the Ancestor of Offerings' tablet in the east-facing position; from the Ancestor of Eminence and Grand Ancestor through all ancestors, follow the left-zhao right-mu array.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Jin Cai Mo: at the October xia, Offerings faces east; Eminence, Grand Ancestor, and the rest follow left-zhao right-mu.

sentences.zh: 此有彰國家重本尚順之明義，足為萬代不易之令典也。

translations.literal: This manifests the state's bright principle of honoring the root and esteeming order—sufficient as an unchanging statute for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: This shows Tang's regard for root and order—a statute for all generations.

sentences.zh: 又議者請奉二祖神主于德明皇帝廟，行祫祭之禮。

translations.literal: Again, deliberators ask to place the two ancestors' tablets in the temple of Emperor Deming and perform xia sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed moving both tablets to the Deming temple for xia.

sentences.zh: 夫祫，合也。

translations.literal: Xia means "combined."
translations.idiomatic: Xia means combined offering.

sentences.zh: 故《公羊傳》云：'大事者何？

translations.literal: Therefore the Gongyang Commentary says: "What is the great affair?
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang asks: "What is the great affair?

sentences.zh: 祫也。

translations.literal: It is xia."
translations.idiomatic: Xia."

sentences.zh: '若祫祭不陳於太廟而享於德明廟，是乃分食也，豈謂合食乎？

translations.literal: If xia sacrifice is not displayed in the Grand Temple but offered in the Deming temple, this is divided feasting—how can it be called combined feasting?
translations.idiomatic: Xia not in the Grand Temple but in the Deming temple is divided feasting, not combined feasting.

sentences.zh: 名實相乖，深失禮意，固不可行也。」

translations.literal: Name and substance cross; it deeply loses ritual intent and absolutely cannot be enacted."
translations.idiomatic: Name and fact diverge—it violates ritual and must be rejected."

sentences.zh: 貞元七年十一月二十八日，太常卿裴鬱奏曰：「禘、祫之禮，殷、周以遷廟皆出太祖之後，故得合食有序，尊卑不差。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month of the seventh Zhenyuan year, Director Pei Yu memorialized: "The rites of di and xia—in Yin and Zhou, because moved temples all came after the Grand Ancestor, combined feasting could be ordered and honor and baseness not err.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan 7, month 11, day 28: Director Pei Yu noted that in Yin and Zhou moved shrines followed the Grand Ancestor, so combined feasting kept order.

sentences.zh: 及漢高受命，無始封祖，以高皇帝為太祖。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu received the mandate, there was no ancestor of first enfeoffment; he took Emperor Gao as Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu had no first-enfeoffment forebear and made Emperor Gao Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太上皇，高帝之父，立廟享祀，不在昭穆合食之列，為尊于太祖故也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Emperor, Gaodi's father, had a temple for offerings—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Emperor, Gaodi's father, had his own temple and stood outside zhao-mu combined feasting as senior to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 魏武創業，文帝受命，亦即以武帝為太祖。

translations.literal: Wei Wu founded the enterprise and Emperor Wen received the mandate; he too took Emperor Wu as Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wu founded the state; Emperor Wen took Emperor Wu as Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 其高皇、太皇、處士君等，並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。

translations.literal: The High Emperor, Grand Emperor, Recluse Lord, and others were all kin seniors—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array.
translations.idiomatic: High Emperor, Grand Emperor, and Recluse Lord were kin seniors outside zhao-mu feasting.

sentences.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。

translations.literal: Jin Xuan founded the enterprise and Emperor Wu received the mandate; he too took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xuan founded the state; Emperor Wu took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 其征西、潁川等四府君，亦為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。

translations.literal: The Western Campaign General, Yingchuan, and the other four lords were also kin seniors—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array.
translations.idiomatic: Western Campaign General, Yingchuan, and three other lords were kin seniors outside zhao-mu feasting.

sentences.zh: 國家誕受天命，累聖重光。

translations.literal: The state received Heaven's mandate; successive sages restored glory.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty received Heaven's mandate through successive sages.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝始封唐公，實為太祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing at first enfeoffment as Duke of Tang was truly the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, was truly Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 中間世數既近，於三昭三穆之內，故皇家太廟，惟有六室。

translations.literal: The generations in between were near; within the three zhao and three mu, so the imperial Grand Temple had only six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Generations were still near; the imperial temple had only six chambers within three zhao and three mu.

sentences.zh: 其弘農府君、宣、光二祖，尊于太祖，親盡則遷，不在昭穆之數。

translations.literal: The Lord of Hongnong and the two ancestors Xuan and Guang, honored above the Grand Ancestor, when kin was exhausted were moved—not in the zhao-mu count.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong Lord and ancestors Xuan and Guang, senior to the Grand Ancestor, moved when kin was exhausted—not in zhao-mu.

sentences.zh: 著在禮志，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Recorded in the ritual monograph—it may be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: This is recorded in the ritual monograph and may be followed.

sentences.zh: 開元中，加置九廟，獻、懿二祖皆在昭穆，是以太祖景皇帝未得居東向之尊。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, nine temples were added; the two ancestors Offerings and Eminence were both in zhao-mu, so Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing could not occupy the east-facing honor.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan added nine temples; Offerings and Eminence entered zhao-mu, so Emperor Jing could not face east.

sentences.zh: 今二祖已祧，九室惟序，則太祖之位又安可不正？

translations.literal: Now the two ancestors have been tithed; the nine chambers are in order only—how can the Grand Ancestor's position again not be corrected?
translations.idiomatic: Now both ancestors are tithed and nine chambers are ordered—how can the Grand Ancestor's seat remain uncorrected?

sentences.zh: 伏乙太祖上配天地，百代不遷，而居昭穆，獻、懿二祖，親盡廟遷，而居東向，征諸故實，實所未安。

translations.literal: Your subject asks: the Grand Ancestor matches Heaven above and is immovable for a hundred generations, yet occupies zhao-mu; the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence, kin exhausted and temples moved, occupy the east-facing position—examined against old facts, this is truly unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor matches Heaven and is immovable, yet sits in zhao-mu while remote Offerings and Eminence face east—this is unsettling.

sentences.zh: 請下百僚僉議。

translations.literal: We ask that deliberation be sent down to the hundred officials for joint discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the hundred officials to deliberate jointly.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨依。

translations.literal: " The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 八年正月二十三日，太子左庶子李嶸等七人議曰：

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day of the first month of the eighth year, Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Li Rong and six others deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Year 8, month 1, day 23: Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Li Rong and six others deliberated:

sentences.zh: 《王制》：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。

translations.literal: The "Royal Regulations": "The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao, three mu, and with the Grand Ancestor, seven."
translations.idiomatic: "Royal Regulations": "The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao, three mu, with the Grand Ancestor, seven."

sentences.zh: 」周制也。

translations.literal: This is the Zhou system.
translations.idiomatic: This is Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 七者，太祖及文王、武王之祧，與親廟四也。

translations.literal: The seven are the Grand Ancestor and the tithes of King Wen and King Wu, with four intimate temples.
translations.idiomatic: Seven means the Grand Ancestor plus Wen and Wu tithes and four intimate temples.

sentences.zh: 太祖，後稷也。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor is Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor is Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 殷則六廟，契及湯與二昭二穆。

translations.literal: Yin had six temples—Qi and Tang with two zhao and two mu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had six: Qi and Tang plus two zhao and two mu.

sentences.zh: 夏則五廟，無太祖，禹與二昭二穆而已。

translations.literal: Xia had five temples, without a Grand Ancestor—Yu with two zhao and two mu only.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had five without Grand Ancestor—Yu plus two zhao and two mu.

sentences.zh: 晉朝博士孫欽議云：「王者受命太祖及諸侯始封之君，其已前神主，據已上數過五代即毀其廟，禘祫不復及也。

translations.literal: Jin Erudite Sun Qin deliberated: "The king receiving the mandate's Grand Ancestor and feudal lords' ancestors of first enfeoffment—for spirit tablets before them, according to the count above, passing five generations destroys the temple; di and xia no longer reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Erudite Sun Qin: tablets before the mandate Grand Ancestor or first-enfeoffment ancestor are destroyed after five generations and excluded from di and xia.

sentences.zh: 禘祫所及者，謂受命太祖之後，迭毀主升藏於二祧者也。

translations.literal: Those reached by di and xia mean after the mandate Grand Ancestor, successively destroyed temples' tablets ascending to storage in the two tithe shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia reach only descendants after the mandate Grand Ancestor, stored in the two tithe shrines.

sentences.zh: 雖百代，禘祫及之。

translations.literal: Even for a hundred generations, di and xia reach them."
translations.idiomatic: Even after a hundred generations di and xia still reach them."

sentences.zh: 」伏以獻、懿二祖，太祖以前親盡之主也。

translations.literal: Your subject notes the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence are tablets of kin exhausted before the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings and Eminence are kin-exhausted forebears before the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 擬三代以降之制，則禘祫不及矣。

translations.literal: Compared with institutions from the Three Dynasties downward, di and xia do not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: By Three Dynasties precedent they are outside di and xia.

sentences.zh: 代祖神主，則太祖已下毀廟之主，則《公羊傳》所謂「已毀廟之主，陳于太祖」者是也。

translations.literal: The tablet of the dynastic ancestor is among tablets of destroyed temples below the Grand Ancestor—this is what the Gongyang Commentary means by "tablets of destroyed temples displayed before the Grand Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic ancestor's tablet is a destroyed-shrine tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor per Gongyang.

sentences.zh: 謹按漢永光四年詔，議罷郡國廟及親盡之祖，丞相韋玄成議太上、孝惠廟，皆親盡宜毀，太上廟主宜瘞於園，孝惠主遷于太祖廟。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to Han Yongguang 4 edict, deliberating abolition of commandery and state temples and ancestors of exhausted kin—Chancellor Wei Xuancheng deliberated the Supreme and Filial Emperor temples, all kin exhausted and fit to destroy; the Supreme temple tablet should be buried in the park, the Filial Emperor tablet moved to the Grand Ancestor temple.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yongguang 4: Wei Xuancheng urged destroying kin-exhausted shrines; the Supreme tablet was buried in the park and Filial Emperor's moved to the Grand Ancestor temple.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: Memorial approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 太上，同太祖已前之主，瘞於園，禘祫不及故也，則今獻、懿二祖之比也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Emperor, like tablets before the Grand Ancestor, buried in the park—di and xia do not reach them; this compares to today's Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Emperor, like pre-Grand Ancestor tablets, was buried in the park and excluded from di and xia—like today's Offerings and Eminence.

sentences.zh: 孝惠遷于太祖廟，明太祖已下子孫，同禘祫所及，則今代祖元皇帝神主之比也。

translations.literal: Filial Emperor moved to the Grand Ancestor temple, showing descendants below the Grand Ancestor share di and xia's reach—this compares to today's dynastic ancestor Emperor Yuan's tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Filial Emperor moved to the Grand Ancestor temple and joined di and xia—like today's Emperor Yuan tablet.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉及宋、齊、陳、隋相承，始受命之君皆立廟，虛太祖之位。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin through Song, Qi, Chen, and Sui in succession, each founding ruler of the mandate established a temple and left the Grand Ancestor's position empty.
translations.idiomatic: Wei through Sui founders each built temples and left the Grand Ancestor seat empty.

sentences.zh: 自太祖之後至七代君，則太祖東向位，乃成七廟。

translations.literal: From after the Grand Ancestor to the seventh-generation ruler, then the Grand Ancestor's east-facing position completed the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after the Grand Ancestor filled the east-facing seat and completed seven temples.

sentences.zh: 太祖以前之主，魏明帝則遷處士主置於園邑，歲時使令丞奉薦，世數猶近故也。

translations.literal: Tablets before the Grand Ancestor—Ming of Wei moved the Recluse Lord's tablet to the park settlement; each year an aide was sent to offer sacrifice, because generations were still near.
translations.idiomatic: Pre-Grand Ancestor tablets: Wei Ming moved the Recluse Lord to the park with seasonal offerings because generations were still near.

sentences.zh: 至東晉明帝崩，以征西等三祖遷入西除，名之曰祧，以准遠廟。

translations.literal: When Ming of Eastern Jin died, the three ancestors including the Western Campaign General were moved into the western side chamber, named tithe, approximating remote temples.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Jin Ming died, three forebears including the Western Campaign General entered the western side chamber as tithe, like remote shrines.

sentences.zh: 至康帝崩，穆帝立，於是京兆遷入西除，同謂之祧，如前之禮，並禘祫所不及。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang died and Emperor Mu succeeded, then Jingzhao was moved into the western side chamber, likewise called tithe; as in the former rite, all were outside di and xia.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kang and Mu, Jingzhao entered the western tithe chamber and, like the earlier case, was excluded from di and xia.

sentences.zh: 國朝始饗四廟，宣、光並太祖、世祖神主祔於廟。

translations.literal: Our dynasty at first feasted at four temples; Xuan and Guang together with the Grand Ancestor and Shizu tablets were enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Tang first had four temples; Xuan and Guang were enshrined with Grand Ancestor and Shizu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，將祔高祖于太廟，硃子奢請准禮立七廟，其三昭三穆，各置神主。

translations.literal: In the ninth Zhenguan year, when Gaozu was to be enshrined in the Grand Temple, Zhu Zishe asked to establish seven temples per the rite—the three zhao and three mu each with a tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 9: enshrining Gaozu, Zhu Zishe asked for seven temples with separate zhao and mu tablets.

sentences.zh: 太祖，依晉宋以來故事，虛其位，待遞遷方處之東向位。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, following Jin-Song precedent, left the position empty, awaiting successive moves to place him in the east-facing seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor seat was left empty per Jin-Song precedent until succession filled the east-facing place.

sentences.zh: 於是始祔弘農府君及高祖為六室，虛太祖之位而行禘祫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hongnong Lord and Gaozu were first enshrined as six chambers; the Grand Ancestor's position was left empty while di and xia were performed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong Lord and Gaozu filled six chambers; the Grand Ancestor seat stayed empty during di and xia.

sentences.zh: 至二十三年，太宗祔廟，弘農府君乃藏於西夾室。

translations.literal: By the twenty-third year, when Taizong was enshrined, the Hongnong Lord was stored in the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Year 23, when Taizong was enshrined, Hongnong Lord went to the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，高宗祔廟，始遷宣皇帝于西夾室。

translations.literal: In the first Weming year, when Gaozong was enshrined, Emperor Xuan was first moved to the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Weming 1, enshrining Gaozong, moved Emperor Xuan to the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，玄宗特立九廟，於是追尊宣皇帝為獻祖，復列於正室，光皇帝為懿祖，以備九室。

translations.literal: In the tenth Kaiyuan year, Xuanzong specially established nine temples; he posthumously honored Emperor Xuan as Ancestor of Offerings, restored to the main chamber, and Emperor Guang as Ancestor of Eminence to complete nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 10: Xuanzong made nine temples, renaming Xuan Offerings and Guang Eminence in the main chambers.

sentences.zh: 禘祫猶虛太祖之位。

translations.literal: Di and xia still left the Grand Ancestor's position empty.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia still left the Grand Ancestor seat empty.

sentences.zh: 祝文于三祖不稱臣，明全廟數而已。

translations.literal: Prayer texts did not call the three ancestors "subject," clarifying that the full temple count alone was intended.
translations.idiomatic: Prayers did not style the three ancestors as subjects—only the full temple count mattered.

sentences.zh: 至德二載克復後，新作九廟神主，遂不造弘農府君神主，明禘祫不及故也。

translations.literal: After recovery in the second Zhide year, new nine-temple tablets were made; the Hongnong Lord tablet was not made, clarifying that di and xia did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide 2 recovery new tablets were made but not for Hongnong Lord—he was outside di and xia.

sentences.zh: 至寶應二年，祔玄宗、肅宗於廟，遷獻、懿二祖於西夾室，始以太祖當東向位，以獻、懿二祖為是太祖以前親盡神主，准禮禘祫不及，凡十八年。

translations.literal: In the second Baoying year, Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined; Offerings and Eminence moved to the western side chamber; only then was the Grand Ancestor placed in the east-facing position, treating Offerings and Eminence as kin-exhausted tablets before the Grand Ancestor—per the rite, di and xia did not reach them—for eighteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying 2: Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined; Offerings and Eminence went to the western side chamber; the Grand Ancestor finally faced east for eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 至建中二年十月，將祫饗，禮儀使顏真卿狀奏：合出獻、懿二祖神主行事，其布位次第及東面尊位，請准東晉蔡謨等議為定。

translations.literal: By the tenth month of the second Jianzhong year, when the xia feast was to be held, Commissioner Yan Zhenqing memorialized that the Offerings and Eminence tablets should be brought out; for array order and the eastern seat of honor, he asked to fix it per Eastern Jin Cai Mo and others' deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong 2, month 10: Yan Zhenqing urged bringing out Offerings and Eminence and fixing placement per Eastern Jin Cai Mo.

sentences.zh: 遂以獻祖當東向，以懿祖于昭位南向，以太祖于穆位北向，以次左昭右穆，陳列行事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ancestor of Offerings faced east, the Ancestor of Eminence in the zhao position facing south, the Grand Ancestor in the mu position facing north, and in sequence left-zhao right-mu for the array.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings faced east, Eminence south in zhao, Grand Ancestor north in mu, with left-zhao right-mu thereafter.

sentences.zh: 且蔡謨當時雖有其議，事竟不行，而我唐廟祧，豈可為准？

translations.literal: Yet though Cai Mo had this deliberation at the time, the affair in the end was not enacted—how can our Tang temple line be taken as standard?
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo's view was never enacted—Tang cannot take it as standard.

sentences.zh: 嶸伏以嘗、禘、郊、社，尊無二上，瘞毀遷藏，禮有義斷。

translations.literal: Rong notes that chang, di, suburban, and altar rites allow no second supreme honor; burial, destruction, relocation, and storage have ritual grounds for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, di, suburban, and altar rites admit no second supreme; burial and relocation follow ritual breaks.

sentences.zh: 以獻、懿為親盡之主，太祖已當東向之尊，一朝改移，實非典故。

translations.literal: Treating Offerings and Eminence as kin-exhausted tablets while the Grand Ancestor should already hold east-facing honor—to shift this in one morning is truly not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings and Eminence are kin-exhausted; the Grand Ancestor should face east—one-morning reversal is not precedent.

sentences.zh: 謂宜復先朝故事，獻、懿神主藏於西夾室，以類《祭法》所謂「遠廟為祧，去祧為壇，去壇為墠，壇、墠有禱則祭，無禱乃止。

translations.literal: We hold the former court's precedent should be restored: Offerings and Eminence tablets stored in the western side chamber, analogous to the Canon of Sacrifices: "Remote temples become tithe; leaving tithe becomes altar; leaving altar becomes open ground; altars and open ground are sacrificed to when there is prayer, otherwise stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Restore precedent: store Offerings and Eminence in the western side chamber like "remote temples become tithe" in the Canon of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」太祖既昭配天地，位當東向之尊。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, having illustriously matched Heaven, should occupy the east-facing honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor, matching Heaven, should face east.

sentences.zh: 庶上守貞觀之首制，中奉開元之成規，下遵寶應之嚴式，符合經義，不失舊章。

translations.literal: Then above one may keep Zhenguan's opening institution, in the middle follow Kaiyuan's completed rule, below observe Baoying's strict form—accordant with canonical meaning, not losing old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhenguan's opening rule, Kaiyuan's settled form, and Baoying's strict practice are all preserved.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中柳冕等十二人議曰：

translations.literal: Supernumerary Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel Liu Mian and twelve others deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian of the Ministry of Personnel and twelve others deliberated:

sentences.zh: 天子受命之君，諸侯始封之祖，皆為太祖。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's ruler who received the mandate and feudal lords' ancestor of first enfeoffment are all called Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The mandate-receiving ruler and a lord's first-enfeoffment ancestor are both Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故雖天子，必有尊也，是以尊太祖焉；

translations.literal: Therefore even the Son of Heaven must have one honored—thus the Grand Ancestor is honored;
translations.idiomatic: Even the Son of Heaven has one who is honored—therefore the Grand Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 故雖諸侯，必有先也，亦以尊太祖焉。

translations.literal: therefore even feudal lords must have forebears—also the Grand Ancestor is honored.
translations.idiomatic: even lords have forebears—also honored as Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故太祖已下，親盡而毀。

translations.literal: Below the Grand Ancestor, when kin is exhausted, temples are destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Grand Ancestor, kin exhaustion destroys temples.

sentences.zh: 洎秦滅學，漢不及禮，不列昭穆，不建迭毀。

translations.literal: By the time Qin extinguished learning, Han did not reach the rites—neither arrayed zhao-mu nor established successive destruction.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin ended learning, Han failed to array zhao-mu or successive destruction.

sentences.zh: 晉失之，宋因之。

translations.literal: Jin lost it; Song followed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lost it.

sentences.zh: 於是有違五廟之制，於是有虛太祖之位。

translations.literal: Thus there was violation of the five-temple system and emptying of the Grand Ancestor's position.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the five-temple rule was violated and the Grand Ancestor seat left empty.

sentences.zh: 夫不列昭穆，非所以示人有序也；

translations.literal: Not arraying zhao-mu is not how to show people there is order;
translations.idiomatic: Failure to array zhao-mu does not show people there is order;

sentences.zh: 不建迭毀，非所以示人有殺也；

translations.literal: Not establishing successive temple removal is not the means to show people that affection diminishes with distance;
translations.idiomatic: Failing to establish successive temple removal is not the way to show that affection diminishes with distance;

sentences.zh: 違五廟之制，非所以示人有別也；

translations.literal: violating the five-temple system is not the means to show people that branches differ;
translations.idiomatic: violating the five-temple system is not the way to show that branches differ;

sentences.zh: 虛太祖之位，非所以示人有尊也。

translations.literal: leaving the Grand Ancestor's seat empty is not the means to show people where honor belongs.
translations.idiomatic: leaving the Grand Ancestor's seat empty is not the way to show where honor belongs.

sentences.zh: 此禮之所由廢。

translations.literal: By this the rite was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the rite fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 按《禮》：「父為士，子為天子，祭以天子，葬以士。

translations.literal: According to the Rites: "When the father was a common officer and the son becomes emperor, sacrifice him with Son-of-Heaven rites but bury him with common-officer rites.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites: "When the father was a common officer and the son becomes emperor, sacrifice him with imperial rites but bury him with common-officer rites.

sentences.zh: 」今獻祖祧也，懿祖亦祧也，唐未受命，猶士禮也。

translations.literal: " Today the Offering Ancestor is in the distant-temple class, the Majestic Ancestor likewise; before Tang received the Mandate, they were still treated with common-officer rites.
translations.idiomatic: " Today Xianzu is in the distant-temple class, Yizu likewise; before Tang received the Mandate, they were still treated with common-officer rites.

sentences.zh: 是故高祖、太宗以天子之禮祭之，不敢以太祖之位易之。

translations.literal: Therefore Gaozu and Taizong sacrificed to them with Son-of-Heaven rites and did not dare displace them into the Grand Ancestor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Gaozu and Taizong sacrificed to them with imperial rites and did not dare displace them into the Grand Ancestor's seat.

sentences.zh: 今而易之，無乃亂先王之序乎？

translations.literal: Now to change this—would it not overturn the order established by former kings?
translations.idiomatic: To change this now—would it not overturn the order established by former kings?

sentences.zh: 昔周有天下，追王太王、王季以天子之禮，及其祭也，親盡而毀之。

translations.literal: In ancient times, when Zhou possessed All under Heaven, it posthumously ennobled Great King and King Ji with Son-of-Heaven rites; when kinship was exhausted in sacrifice, their temples were removed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Zhou possessed the realm, it posthumously ennobled Great King and King Ji with imperial rites; when kinship was exhausted in sacrifice, their temples were removed.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，尊太上皇以天子之禮，及其祭也，親盡而毀之。

translations.literal: When Han possessed All under Heaven, it honored the Supreme Emperor with Son-of-Heaven rites; when kinship was exhausted, his temple was removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Han possessed the realm, it honored the Supreme Emperor with imperial rites; when kinship was exhausted, his temple was removed.

sentences.zh: 唐有天下，追王獻、懿二祖以天子之禮，及其祭也，親盡而毀之。

translations.literal: When Tang possessed All under Heaven, it posthumously ennobled the Offering and Majestic ancestors with Son-of-Heaven rites; when kinship was exhausted, their temples were removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang possessed the realm, it posthumously ennobled the Offering and Majestic ancestors with imperial rites; when kinship was exhausted, their temples were removed.

sentences.zh: 則不可代太祖之位明矣。

translations.literal: It is clear that they cannot take the Grand Ancestor's place.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly they cannot take the Grand Ancestor's place.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮》有先公之祧，有先王之祧。

translations.literal: Again, in the Rites of Zhou of Zhou distinguish distant temples for former lords and distant temples for former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Rites of Zhou distinguish distant temples for former lords and distant temples for former kings.

sentences.zh: 先公之遷主，藏乎後稷之廟，其周未受命之祧乎？

translations.literal: The migrated tablets of former lords removed from their halls were stored in Hou Ji's temple—were these Zhou's distant temples before receiving the Mandate?
translations.idiomatic: Tablets of former lords removed from their halls were stored in Hou Ji's temple—were these Zhou's distant temples before receiving the Mandate?

sentences.zh: 先王之遷主，藏乎文王之廟，其周已受命之祧乎？

translations.literal: The migrated tablets of former kings were stored in King Wen's temple—were these Zhou's distant temples after receiving the Mandate?
translations.idiomatic: Tablets of former kings were stored in King Wen's temple—were these Zhou's distant temples after receiving the Mandate?

sentences.zh: 故有二祧，所以異廟也。

translations.literal: Therefore the two distant temples served to distinguish different temple lines.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the two distant temples served to distinguish different temple lines.

sentences.zh: 今獻祖已下之祧，猶先公也；

translations.literal: Today the distant temples from the Offering Ancestor downward correspond to the former-lord class;
translations.idiomatic: Today the distant temples from Xianzu downward correspond to the former-lord class;

sentences.zh: 太祖已下之祧，猶先王也。

translations.literal: Those from the Grand Ancestor downward correspond to the former-king class.
translations.idiomatic: those from the Grand Ancestor downward correspond to the former-king class.

sentences.zh: 請築別廟以居二祖，則行周之禮，復古之道。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that separate temples be built to house the two ancestors, thus practicing Zhou rites and restoring the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that separate temples be built to house the two ancestors, thus practicing Zhou rites and restoring the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 故漢之禮，因于周也；

translations.literal: Thus the Han rites were arrayed Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Han rites followed Zhou;

sentences.zh: 魏之禮，因於漢也；

translations.literal: Wei rites were arrayed Han;
translations.idiomatic: Wei rites followed Han;

sentences.zh: 隋之禮，因于魏也。

translations.literal: Sui rites were arrayed Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sui rites followed Wei.

sentences.zh: 皆立三廟，有二祧。

translations.literal: Each established three temples, with two distant temples.
translations.idiomatic: All established three temples with two distant temples.

sentences.zh: 又立私廟四於南陽，亦後漢制也。

translations.literal: They also set up four private temples at Nanyang, likewise a Later Han institution.
translations.idiomatic: They also established four private temples at Nanyang, likewise a Later Han institution.

sentences.zh: 以為人之子，事大宗降其私親，故私廟所以奉本宗也。

translations.literal: The idea is that as a man's son, one serves the great lineage and lowers one's private kin; hence private temples serve the root lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The idea is that as a man's son, one serves the great lineage and subordinates private kin; hence private temples serve the root lineage.

sentences.zh: 太廟所以尊正統也。

translations.literal: The the Grand Temple honors the orthodox succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Temple honors the orthodox succession.

sentences.zh: 雖古今異時，文質異禮，而右禮之情，與問禮之本者，莫不通其變，酌而行之。

translations.literal: Though ancient and modern times differ in time and rites differ in refinement, those who uphold ritual feeling and inquire into ritual roots all penetrate its changes and weigh what to enact.
translations.idiomatic: Though ancient and modern differ in time and rites differ in refinement, those who uphold ritual feeling and inquire into ritual roots all penetrate its changes and weigh what to enact.

sentences.zh: 故上致其崇，則太祖屬尊乎上矣；

translations.literal: Thus, in elevating what is honored above, the Grand Ancestor is set in honor above;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in elevating what is honored above, the Grand Ancestor is set in honor above;

sentences.zh: 下盡其殺，則祧主親盡於下矣；

translations.literal: In exhausting diminution below, distant-temple tablets are exhausted in kinship below;
translations.idiomatic: in exhausting diminution below, distant-temple tablets are exhausted in kinship below;

sentences.zh: 中處其中，則王者主祧於中矣。

translations.literal: And in taking the middle position between them, the Son of Heaven holds the distant temples in the center.
translations.idiomatic: and in taking the middle position between them, the Son of Heaven holds the distant temples in the center.

translations.literal: Supervisor of Works Zhang Jian and others submitted: "Formerly Yin and Zhou took Qi and Xun as the first enfeoffed ancestors who were not removed; tablets of destroyed temples were all descendants of Qi and Xun, so zhao and mu were offered together and honor and baseness did not err.

translations.idiomatic: As the Xia took Yu as first enfeoffed, he became the ancestor not removed.

translations.idiomatic: Hence the Xia's five temples were only Yu with two zhao and two mu.

sentences.zh: 據此則鯀之親盡，其主已遷。

translations.literal: Thereupon, Gun's kinship was exhausted and his tablet was already removed.
translations.idiomatic: From this, Gun's kinship was exhausted and his tablet was already removed.

sentences.zh: 左氏既稱'禹不先鯀'，足明遷廟之主，中屬尊于始封祖者，亦在合食之位矣。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary likewise states "Yu did not precede Gun," enough to show that among removed tablets, those in the middle honored above the first enfeoffed ancestor also held places in the joint offering.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary also says "Yu did not precede Gun," sufficient to show that among removed tablets, those in the middle honored above the first enfeoffed ancestor also held places in the joint offering.

sentences.zh: 又據晉、宋、齊、梁、北齊、周、隋史，其太祖已下，並同禘祫，未嘗限斷遷毀之主。

translations.literal: Again, Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Northern Qi, Zhou, and Sui histories show that from the Grand Ancestor downward all shared di and he sacrifices alike, never limiting removed and destroyed tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Again, Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Northern Qi, Zhou, and Sui histories show that from the Grand Ancestor downward all shared di and he alike, never limiting removed and destroyed tablets.

sentences.zh: 伏以南北八代，非無碩學巨儒，宗廟大事，議必精博，驗於史冊，其禮僉同。

translations.literal: We respectfully submit that across eight dynasties north and south there were great scholars; on great matters of the ancestral temples deliberation was surely thorough—verified in histories, their rites were unanimous.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that across eight dynasties north and south there were great scholars; on great matters of the ancestral temples deliberation was surely thorough—verified in histories, their rites were unanimous.

sentences.zh: 又詳魏、晉、宋、齊、梁、北齊、周、隋故事，及《貞觀》、《顯慶》、《開元禮》所述，禘袷並虛東向。

translations.literal: Again, examining Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Northern Qi, Zhou, and Sui precedents and what the Zhenguan, Xianqing, and Kaiyuan Rites describe, di and he sacrifices alike left the east-facing seat vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Again, examining Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Northern Qi, Zhou, and Sui precedents and what the Zhenguan, Xianqing, and Kaiyuan Rites describe, di and he alike left the east-facing seat vacant.

sentences.zh: 既行之已久，實群情所安。

translations.literal: Having long been practiced long, it truly settles popular feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Having been practiced long, it truly settles popular feeling.

translations.literal: Moreover, the Grand Ancestor occupies the first chamber of the clear temple; though his tablet is not removed for a hundred generations and forever receives seasonal offerings, matching Heaven and Earth on high, in suburban and temple rites nothing is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Grand Ancestor occupies the first chamber of the clear temple; though his tablet is not removed for a hundred generations and forever receives seasonal offerings, matching Heaven and Earth above, in suburban and temple rites nothing is not correct.

translations.idiomatic: If at di and he times he temporarily takes a place in the zhao-mu array, lowering himself to extend filial piety and serve ancestors, is this not the way of Yu earnestly revering Gun?

sentences.zh: 亦是魏、晉及周、隋之太祖，不敢以卑厭尊之義也。

translations.literal: This is also the meaning by which Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui Grand Ancestors did not dare use the low to disdain the high.
translations.idiomatic: It is also the meaning by which Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui Grand Ancestors did not dare use the low to disdain the high.

sentences.zh: 議者或欲遷二祖於興聖廟，及請別置築室，至禘祫年饗之。

translations.literal: Some debaters wish to move the two ancestors to the Xingsheng Temple, or request separate chambers built and offered at di and he sacrifices years.
translations.idiomatic: Some debaters wish to move the two ancestors to the Xingsheng Temple, or request separate chambers built and offered at di and he years.

sentences.zh: 夫祫，合也。

translations.idiomatic: He means "union."

translations.idiomatic: This would be divided offerings, greatly at odds with ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 又欲藏於西夾室，永不及祀，無異漢代瘞園，尤為不可。

translations.literal: Others wish to store them in the west side chambers, never attaining sacrifice—no different from Han burial in the garden, especially impossible.

translations.literal: We venture to cite the canonical classics, examine old histories, and ask that the Offering and Majestic ancestors join the Grand Ancestor in the zhao and mu places while the east-facing seat remains vacant."
translations.idiomatic: We venture to cite the canonical classics, examine old histories, and ask that the Offering and Majestic ancestors join the Grand Ancestor in the zhao-mu places while the east-facing seat remains vacant."

translations.literal: Director of Merit in the Ministry Pei Shu presented: "Rites must establish a lineage head to gather the clan; the east-facing lord is likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Merit Pei Shu submitted: "Rites must establish a lineage head to gather the clan; the east-facing lord is likewise so.

sentences.zh: 若祔於遠廟，無乃中有一間，等上不倫。

translations.literal: If they are enshrined in a distant temple, would there not be a gap in the middle, unequal above and not of one kind?
translations.idiomatic: If enshrined in a distant temple, would there not be a gap in the middle, unequal above and not of one kind?

sentences.zh: 西位常虛，則太祖永厭于昭穆；

translations.literal: If the west place is always vacant, the Grand Ancestor is forever displeased in zhao and mu;
translations.idiomatic: If the west place is always vacant, the Grand Ancestor is forever displeased in zhao-mu;

sentences.zh: 異廟別祭，則祫饗何主乎合食？

translations.literal: If separate temples have separate offerings, at he feasting what lord unites the joint meal?
translations.idiomatic: if separate temples have separate offerings, at he feasting what lord unites the joint meal?

sentences.zh: 永閟比于薑嫄，則推祥禖而無事。

translations.literal: Forever to close them like Jiang Yuan, then pushing auspicious and dire omens with nothing to do.
translations.idiomatic: Forever closing them like Jiang Yuan, then pushing auspicious and dire omens with nothing to do.

translations.literal: The Rites state: "Cherish kin therefore honor ancestors, honor ancestors therefore respect the lineage head, respect the lineage head therefore gather the clan"—hence ancestral temples are strict and altars of soil and grain are weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "Cherish kin therefore honor ancestors, honor ancestors therefore respect the lineage head, respect the lineage head therefore gather the clan"—hence ancestral temples are strict and altars of soil and grain are weighty.

sentences.zh: '由是言也，太祖之上復有追尊之祖，則親親尊祖之義，無乃乖乎？

translations.literal: ' Thereupon it follows that above the Grand Ancestor there are again posthumously honored ancestors—would not the meaning of cherishing kin and honoring ancestors be violated?
translations.idiomatic: ' From this it follows that above the Grand Ancestor there are again posthumously honored ancestors—would not the meaning of cherishing kin and honoring ancestors be violated?

sentences.zh: 太廟之外，輕置別祭之廟，則宗廟無乃不嚴，社稷無乃不重乎？

translations.literal: Outside the Grand Temple, lightly to set separate offering temples—would ancestral temples not be lax and altars of soil and grain not be light?
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Grand Temple lightly to set separate offering temples—would ancestral temples not be lax and altars of soil and grain not be light?

sentences.zh: 且漢丞相韋玄成請瘞于園，晉征士虞喜請瘞於廟兩階之間。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Han chancellor Wei Xuancheng asked to bury in the garden; Jin recluse Yu Xi asked to bury in the space between the temple stairways.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han Chancellor Wei Xuancheng asked to bury in the garden; Jin recluse Yu Xi asked to bury in the space between the temple stairways.

sentences.zh: 喜又引左氏說，古者先王日祭于祖考，月祀于曾高，時享及二祧，歲祫及壇墠，終禘及郊宗石室。

translations.literal: Xi also cited the Zuo Commentary: in antiquity former kings daily sacrificed to ancestors and fathers, monthly to great-great-grandfathers, seasonal offerings including the two distant temples, yearly he including altars and mounds, final di including suburban, ancestral, and stone-chamber spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Xi also cited the Zuo Commentary: ancient former kings daily sacrificed to ancestors and fathers, monthly to great-great-grandfathers, seasonal offerings including the two distant temples, yearly he including altars and mounds, final di including suburban, ancestral, and stone-chamber spirits.

sentences.zh: 是謂郊宗之上，復有石室之祖，斯最近矣。

translations.literal: This means that above the suburban ancestral spirit there is again the stone-chamber ancestor—this is nearest in kinship.
translations.idiomatic: This means above the suburban ancestral spirit there is again the stone-chamber ancestor—this is nearest in kinship.

sentences.zh: 但當時議所居石室，未有准的。

translations.literal: But when they deliberated where the stone chamber should stand, there was no standard.
translations.idiomatic: But when they debated where the stone chamber should stand, there was no standard.

sentences.zh: 喜請於夾室中，愚以為石室可據，所以處之之道未安。

translations.literal: Xi asked to place it in the side chambers; your servant deems the stone chamber can be cited, but the way to situate it is not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xi asked to place it in the side chambers; I deem the stone chamber can be cited, but the way to situate it is not settled.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: For what reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夾室謂居太祖之下毀主，非是安太祖之上藏主也。

translations.literal: Side chambers signify placing removed tablets below the Grand Ancestor, not installing tablets above the Grand Ancestor in storage.
translations.idiomatic: Side chambers mean placing removed tablets below the Grand Ancestor, not installing tablets above the Grand Ancestor in storage.

sentences.zh: 未有卑處正位，尊在傍居。

translations.literal: Never has the humble occupied the correct position while the honored dwells at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Never has the low occupied the correct position while the honored dwells at the side.

sentences.zh: 考理即心，恐非允協。

translations.literal: On examining reason and the heart, I fear it is not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Examining reason and the heart, I fear it is not acceptable.

sentences.zh: 今若建石室於園寢，遷神主以永安，采漢、晉之舊章，仍禘袷之一祭，修古禮之殘缺，為國朝之典故，庶乎《春秋》變禮之正，動也中者焉。」
